items.title: IEA launches one-year project to support Ghana’s Nuclear Power Programme
items.description: The Institute of Economic Affairs (IEA Ghana), through its Nuclear Energy Centre of Excellence, has launched a one-year initiative aimed at supporting selected priority activities under Phase Two of Ghana’s Nuclear Power Programme. The initiative, titled the Ghana Nuclear Phase II Completion and Investment Readiness Support Programme, is designed to strengthen institutional coordination, human resource capacity, regulatory preparedness and the policy and investment frameworks necessary to advance Ghana’s nuclear power ambitions. Acording to the IEA, the programme represents an important contribution to ongoing national efforts to address outstanding nuclear infrastructure requirements and strengthen the country’s preparedness for critical decisions concerning the development of its first nuclear power plant. Ghana is currently implementing Phase Two of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) Milestones Approach, a structured framework that guides countries developing nuclear power programmes through the institutional, technical, regulatory and financial preparations required for the safe, secure and sustainable introduction of nuclear electricity generation. Having completed Phase One, the IEA said Ghana is working towards fulfilling the requirements of the second milestone, which concerns national readiness to invite bids or negotiate a contract for its first nuclear power plant. “Although Ghana has made considerable progress in establishing the foundations for its nuclear energy programme, the transition towards implementation requires sustained attention to institutional effectiveness, technical preparedness, financing arrangements, regulatory capacity and coordination among the organisations responsible for delivering the programme”, it stated. The IEA said its initiative seeks to contribute to these efforts through targeted policy research, technical engagement, institutional assessments, stakeholder consultations and practical decision support instruments. Strengthening Coordination and Institutional Readiness The IEA stressed that a central component of the project will focus on strengthening governance and institutional coordination across Ghana’s nuclear power development ecosystem. “The introduction of nuclear power requires effective collaboration among government ministries, implementing institutions, the nuclear regulatory authority, electricity-sector organisations, technical agencies and other relevant stakeholders”. Therefore, it noted that the project will support the identification of critical implementation priorities, institutional responsibilities, coordination requirements and potential obstacles affecting the completion of Phase Two activities. Through structured engagements with relevant institutions, the policy think-tank said the initiative is expected to contribute to clearer implementation priorities, improved information sharing and the development of practical mechanisms for monitoring progress against national nuclear infrastructure requirements. Supporting Human Resource Development The project will also examine Ghana’s human resource and competency requirements for the next stages of nuclear power development. The IEA said the nuclear energy infrastructure requires a highly specialised workforce spanning engineering, nuclear safety, security, regulation, project management, environmental assessment, safeguards, finance and other technical and professional disciplines. Therefore, the initiative will assess priority human capacity requirements and support the development of a workforce planning framework that identifies existing capabilities, critical competency gaps and opportunities for coordinated training and professional development. It added that particular attention will be given to strengthening the sustainability of Ghana’s nuclear workforce and ensuring that capacity-building efforts remain aligned with the evolving responsibilities of national institutions.

items.title: Africa CDC urges coordinated action as Ebola outbreak exceeds 10,000 cases
items.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has urged African countries to strengthen cross-border cooperation and coordinate their responses as an Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus continues to spread beyond the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The call was made at an extraordinary virtual meeting of African health ministers on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, where participants discussed measures to strengthen surveillance, improve preparedness and accelerate efforts to contain the outbreak. According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the outbreak had recorded 10,172 confirmed cases and 4,932 confirmed deaths across five affected countries and territories as of October 26. The DRC accounted for the overwhelming majority of the cases and deaths. The outbreak, which began in the DRC in May 2026, has also been reported in Kenya and Nigeria, while Uganda and France have recorded cases associated with the wider outbreak. The CDC has described it as the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, behind the 2014–2016 West African epidemic. Africa CDC Director-General Dr Jean Kaseya said the outbreak was affecting more than public health, with consequences for trade, supply chains and household livelihoods. “Trade is disrupted, supply chains are broken, and we are seeing a tragic loss of breadwinners. This is not just a health crisis; it is an economic destabilizer for our communities,” he said. The meeting brought together representatives of African governments and international organisations to discuss a coordinated response, including improved surveillance, information sharing and preparedness across national borders. South Africa’s Director-General for Health, Simbisile Kulu, speaking on behalf of the country’s Health Minister, Dr Motsualedi, described the spread of the outbreak beyond the DRC as a continental health security concern. She said South Africa was strengthening surveillance, laboratory capacity, infection prevention and control, contact tracing and preparedness at its borders. She also called for stronger regional operational readiness, harmonised alert protocols and real-time information sharing to help countries respond more effectively. Ethiopia expressed readiness to deploy teams and cooperate with neighbouring countries on border screening, information sharing and transport. Niger, meanwhile, outlined measures to strengthen surveillance, laboratory capacity, isolation arrangements, staff training and coordination across sectors. The discussions emphasised the need for countries to align their response plans and share information promptly to detect and contain potential cross-border transmission. India reaffirmed its commitment to supporting the response, reporting US$10 million in in-kind medical assistance and supplies, including laboratory materials, essential medicines and nutritional support. Its representative outlined deliveries to Uganda and Kenya, including 2.5 tonnes of supplies to Uganda on May 24, followed by another 43 tonnes on June 2. Kenya received five tonnes of supplies on July 22, while more than 11 tonnes of medical supplies and specialised equipment were delivered on October 19. India also highlighted its cooperation with African institutions in research and development, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory harmonisation and digital health. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) called for a One Health approach, which recognises the links between human, animal and environmental health. The organisation said it was supporting animal and wildlife disease surveillance, early-warning systems, laboratory capacity and the provision of protective equipment. It also cited assistance to communities in Eastern Africa through agricultural inputs and cash support. The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) highlighted the effects of the outbreak on women and girls, particularly frontline health workers and caregivers. Its representative said the agency had mobilised US$2.8 million in emergency funding and was supporting triage, reproductive health services, dignity supplies and risk communication. UNICEF representative Alison Parker drew attention to the impact on children, reporting that more than 2,000 children had been affected and more than 1,100 had died during the period under review. She also noted that children under five faced a higher risk of severe outcomes. Participants called for the deployment of African health experts and sustainable financing to support countries responding to the outbreak. They also stressed the importance of strengthening surveillance at border crossings, improving screening at points of entry, protecting frontline health workers and engaging communities in prevention efforts. The meeting forms part of wider efforts to reinforce continental health security and prevent further transmission. Africa CDC has urged member states to maintain vigilance and strengthen cooperation as the response continues.

items.title: ‘I won’t waste my time talking about Amaechi’ — Oshiomhole
items.description: Senator Adams Oshiomhole has dismissed former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as unreliable, saying he would not waste his time discussing the former minister. Oshiomhole spoke on TVC while reacting to Amaechi’s comments that President Bola Tinubu faces more challengers in the 2027 presidential election top challengers are from the South, while former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has fewer opponents because he is from the North. “If you know Amaechi, you won’t waste airtime talking about him,” Oshiomhole said. The former Edo State governor questioned Amaechi’s political consistency, citing his past dispute with Atiku over the African Democratic Congress presidential primary. According to Oshiomhole, Amaechi had accused Atiku of emerging from a fraudulent primary and challenged his victory in court. “Here is Amaechi on record in your TVC coverage and other network stations, who said that his own boss, the presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, that the primary that produce him was a fraudulent process, and Atiku stole the mandate, he didn’t win the mandate. He didn’t stop there. Amaechi went to court to challenge Atiku that he stole the mandate,” he said. Oshiomhole added that Atiku later reached an agreement with Amaechi, claiming the former vice-president had asked him to share the mandate they allegedly obtained through a fraudulent process. “This is not social media, there are court documents, and Atiku went back to him and said okay, let’s share the stolen mandate together,” he said. Oshiomhole also referred to Amaechi’s political history, arguing that his rise to power and appointment as a minister were not the result of direct electoral victories. He said Amaechi became governor following a Supreme Court decision and was appointed minister by former President Muhammadu Buhari in 2015. “And I am not surprised that knowing what I know about him…he’s been very lucky that Supreme Court make him a governor without appearing on the ballot, and President Buhari made him a minister without voting for him in 2015, because I was a national player and later national chairman, so I know what I’m talking about,” Oshiomhole said. The senator further criticised Amaechi for describing other political figures as ethnic champions, arguing that the former governor had presented himself as the exception before the African Democratic Congress primaries. “He referred to Atiku as an ethnic champion. He referred to every other person as an ethnic champion. He was the only non-ethnic champion in the ADC before their primaries,” Oshiomhole said. He questioned Amaechi’s assessment of other political leaders, saying someone who dismisses others as ethnic champions should not be taken seriously when discussing leadership in a diverse country like Nigeria. The post ‘I won’t waste my time talking about Amaechi’ — Oshiomhole appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kamsar : la CBG et l’AJDEF célèbrent le Mois de l’enfant autour de ses droits fondamentaux
items.description: La Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée (CBG), en partenariat avec l’ONG Assistance Justice aux Droits des Enfants et Femmes (AJDEF), a officiellement lancé, ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026, les activités de sensibilisation et de promotion des droits de l’enfant au centre de loisirs de la CBG, à Dougouffissa, dans la préfecture de Kamsar. Organisée en différé dans le cadre du Mois de l’enfant, cette initiative vise à renforcer la sensibilisation sur les droits fondamentaux des enfants, notamment dans les zones d’intervention de la compagnie, à savoir Kamsar, Boké et Sangarédi. Cette année, le thème retenu par l’Union africaine met l’accent sur la nécessité de « garantir l’accès universel à l’eau, à l’assainissement et à l’hygiène pour chaque enfant en Afrique ». La cérémonie a été présidée par Alsény Barry, chef de cabinet du gouvernorat de Boké, en présence de la préfète de Kamsar, le lieutenant-colonel Dja Doumbouya, des autorités locales, des responsables de la CBG et de l’ANAIM, des représentants de l’ONG AJDEF ainsi que de nombreux enfants. Dans son discours de bienvenue, la préfète de Kamsar, le lieutenant-colonel Dja Doumbouya, a salué l’engagement de la direction générale de la CBG et de l’ONG AJDEF en faveur de la promotion et de la protection des droits de l’enfant. Elle a souligné l’importance de cette initiative, particulièrement au regard du thème retenu cette année, qui met en lumière les enjeux liés à l’accès à l’eau potable, à l’assainissement et à l’hygiène pour tous les enfants. Cette activité s’inscrit également dans le cadre des actions de responsabilité sociétale de la CBG en faveur des communautés riveraines de ses zones d’opération. Prenant la parole au nom de la direction générale de la CBG, Pierre Dominique Traoré, directeur du Groupe stratégique Développement qualité, représentant le directeur général, Maître Karifa Condé, a rappelé l’importance de cette célébration pour la compagnie. « Pour la Compagnie des Bauxites de Guinée, cette initiative traduit notre engagement sociétal et notre volonté de contribuer durablement au bien-être des communautés vivant dans nos zones d’opération », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également insisté sur la place centrale de l’enfant dans la construction de l’avenir du pays. « L’enfant représente l’avenir de notre pays et mérite de grandir dans un environnement sain, sécurisé, inclusif et favorable à son épanouissement. La protection de ses droits, de sa dignité et de son avenir constitue donc une responsabilité collective à laquelle nous devons tous prendre part », a-t-il souligné. De son côté, Alsény Barry, chef de cabinet du gouvernorat de Boké, a salué et remercié la direction générale de la CBG pour les différentes initiatives menées en faveur des communautés de la région. Il a rappelé que le lancement en différé des activités du Mois de l’enfant constitue une occasion importante de mobiliser les acteurs institutionnels, les organisations de la société civile et les communautés autour de la protection des enfants et du respect de leurs droits. Cette mobilisation témoigne, selon lui, de la nécessité d’une action collective pour garantir aux enfants un environnement propice à leur épanouissement et à leur développement. La cérémonie s’est achevée dans une ambiance festive, marquée par des prestations de danse et des interventions d’enfants, qui ont exprimé leur attachement à la protection de leurs droits. À travers cette activité organisée en partenariat avec l’AJDEF, la CBG réaffirme sa volonté de poursuivre ses actions de sensibilisation et d’accompagnement des communautés, en mettant l’accent sur le bien-être, la dignité et la protection des enfants.

items.title: Israel piles pressure on Arab parties as Netanyahu seeks government
items.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc on Thursday piled pressure on Israeli Arab leaders over unproven accusations of foreign funding, in a push to neuter parties that could hold the key to forming a government after an inconclusive election. Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for an investigation into allegations of fraud but cautioned against stigmatising the entire Arab Israeli community, who voted at unprecedented rates. Israel was nearing the completion of ballot-counting from Tuesday’s election , in which neither Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot looked able to secure a majority in the parliament known as the Knesset. The Netanyahu camp’s accusations, which a key Arab party has rejected, could bring uncertainty to the electoral process at a time when the threat of a return to war with Iran looms over the region. Israel’s election saw soaring participation by Israeli Arabs , descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the country’s creation in 1948, as outrage boiled at calls by officials such as National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir to treat their community much as Israel has dealt with Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank. Following Netanyahu’s accusations of impropriety, Ben Gvir went so far as to encourage Israel to “immediately” order the arrests of Arab party leaders. Raam party leader Mansour Abbas said he welcomed an investigation into claims of wrongdoing, adding that his party had “no connection” with the accusations. The Arab parties together have enough votes to take the opposition bloc over the finish line, but Eisenkot has baulked after relentless attacks by Netanyahu, who warned his right-wing Jewish base that voting for the opposition would put Arabs in power. ‘Political earthquake’ Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, a conservative who heads the Central Election Commission, requested an investigation by the Shin Bet security service into allegations that Raam received money from Qatar. “The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said. Government officials did not offer evidence to back the allegations, and left-wing candidate Yair Golan accused Netanyahu of attempting to stir controversy after failing to get a majority. “Now he is trying to challenge the election results through an ugly delegitimisation campaign against the will of the people, and against the Arab public in particular.” Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state. Meanwhile, Qatar’s foreign ministry spokesman on Thursday rejected accusations “made by certain Israeli politicians and their contacts in the media” that his country had interfered in the Israeli elections. “We categorically deny allegations that Qatar has interfered in Israeli elections or funded any activities intended to influence their outcome,” said Majed Al Ansari. “They accuse Qatar of buying off Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli political left and now, in this latest campaign, the Arab vote […] These accusations are ridiculous and dangerous in equal measure.” Kingmakers under pressure With nearly 93 per cent of the vote counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was at 53 seats and the opposition forces led by Eisenkot on 48 — both well under the 61 needed to form a government. The two main Arab formations were on track for an unprecedented 19 seats between them. Some observers quickly said that the allegations would help Netanyahu by making the Arab lawmakers even more toxic to Eisenkot. Yousef Jabareen, the head of the leftist Arab-majority Joint List, told AFP on Wednesday that he was willing to cooperate with the opposition to bring down Netanyahu but without joining it in a government. In response to the new allegations, Eisenkot said he was receiving updates and promised “utmost vigilance” against election interference. “On the other hand, we cannot allow political actors to exploit the situation and influence the timing of the inauguration of the 26th Knesset,” he said. One of Eisenkot’s right-leaning allies, Avigdor Lieberman, called the allegations “dramatic and unprecedented” and urged a swift investigation. An Israeli police statement said that they would investigate every complaint about election integrity. The great survivor Netanyahu, who has led Israel on and off for more than 19 years, is known as a wily political operator. He tried on Tuesday to raise allegations of fraud, saying that Arab parties were caught with envelopes of cash, and his Likud party peddled the accusations throughout Thursday. Police said they arrested three suspects but the election commission called it an isolated local case. Another factor that could play into the formation of a government is an attack on Iran . Netanyahu has repeatedly threatened to strike Iran, with his ally US President Donald Trump signalling he was ready to attack after next Tuesday’s US midterm elections, in which his Republican Party is forecast to lose ground. Eisenkot has warned the military that Netanyahu has no mandate and that officers must put Israel’s security over the premier’s “political needs”. An attack could raise pressure on Eisenkot to join an emergency unity government, an option he has publicly ruled out, or keep the clock running until Israel can call new elections. President Herzog will decide after the publication of the official results which person to task with a first chance of forming a government. Palestinian president says hopes for peace talks with new govt Meanwhile, Palestinian president Mahmoud Abbas said on Thursday that he hoped the election of a new Israeli government would allow for the resumption of peace talks. “For many years now, we have been extending a hand to the Israeli side in order to achieve peace with them, so that Israel and Palestine may live in security, stability and peace,” Abbas said during a meeting with Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides in Nicosia. “We hope that, immediately after a new Israeli government is formed, we will be able to engage in dialogue together,” he added. The Israeli-Palestinian peace process has been stalled for years, despite the recognition of the State of Palestine by a growing number of countries. Under Netanyahu’s watch, settlement construction and violence against Palestinians has soared in the occupied West Bank, where Abbas’ Palestinian Authority exercises limited self-rule.

items.title: Terrorists kill police inspector, 11 civilians in Kebbi
items.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi Suspected Mamudawa/Lakurawa terrorists have killed a police inspector and 11 civilians in attacks on Waiwayi and Kystu villages in Koko/Besse Local Government Area of Kebbi State. The Kebbi State Police Command confirmed the killings, saying the police inspector died during an exchange of fire with the attackers. The command’s spokesperson, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a telephone conversation with our correspondent. Usman said the inspector’s identity had yet to be released pending the conclusion of investigations. “Yes, there was an attack on the villages of Waiwayi and Kystu by suspected Mamudawa, and unfortunately, during an exchange of fire, they killed one police inspector. I can’t give you his name yet till we finish investigation,” he said. The attackers were also reported to have set houses ablaze and looted food items from shops in the affected communities. The attacks forced surviving residents to flee their homes in search of safety. Usman said the police and other security agencies had cordoned off the affected areas to prevent further attacks. He added that security operatives had launched a manhunt for the assailants. The incident adds to security concerns in parts of Kebbi State, where attacks on rural communities have threatened lives, livelihoods and residents’ safety. items.title: Imo West: South-East Youths congratulate Okorocha, urge Uzodimma to respect the ruling
items.description: By Chinedu Adonu The South-East Youths Stakeholders Forum has congratulated former Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha, following a Federal High Court judgment declaring him the winner of the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial primary for Imo West ahead of the 2027 general elections. The forum also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to comply with the court’s directives and take the necessary steps to recognise Okorocha as the party’s candidate for the district. The judgment, delivered on Thursday by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, ordered Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State to stop presenting himself as the APC candidate for the Imo West senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. The court held that evidence before it established that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast during the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026, which was monitored by INEC. It consequently directed the APC to submit Okorocha’s name to the electoral commission as its candidate for the election. The ruling followed a legal challenge by Okorocha against Uzodimma’s recognition as the party’s candidate. INEC’s previously reported official results had listed Uzodimma as the winner of the primary, a position Okorocha contested in court. Reacting to the judgment, the forum described the development as significant and expressed confidence that the rule of law would prevail in resolving political disputes. In a statement made available to journalists, the chairman of the forum’s Imo State chapter, Comrade Ifeanyi Nwosu, said respect for judicial decisions remained fundamental to democracy, justice, peace and political stability. The forum called on INEC to take the necessary steps to implement the judgment in accordance with the court’s directives and applicable laws. It also appealed to Uzodimma and his supporters to respect the ruling, embrace reconciliation and work towards a united APC ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to the group, unity, mutual understanding and collective commitment among party leaders and stakeholders are essential to strengthening the APC and advancing its electoral objectives. The forum further reaffirmed its commitment to mobilising youths across the South-East in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and APC candidates in future elections. It urged party leaders and stakeholders in Imo State to set aside their differences and work together in the interest of the party. items.title: Ghana’s Sam George unanimously elected Chair of AU ICT Committee for two years
items.description: Ghana’s Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, has been unanimously confirmed as Chairperson of the African Union’s Specialised Technical Committee on Communication and Information and Communications Technology (AU STC-CICT) for a two-year term beginning in October 2026. The unanimous confirmation, secured at the committee’s ministerial session in Libreville, Gabon, places Ghana at the forefront of continental efforts to advance digital transformation, strengthen cybersecurity cooperation and promote Africa’s interests in the rapidly evolving global digital economy. Accepting the chairmanship, Samuel Nartey George described the appointment as a responsibility to the entire African Union rather than a privilege for Ghana alone. He expressed appreciation to the Government and people of Gabon for hosting the meeting, while commending the outgoing chairperson, Lesotho’s Minister for Information, Communication, Science, Technology and Innovation, Nthati Morosi, and the outgoing bureau for their stewardship. The Ghanaian Minister pledged to build on the committee’s existing work, stressing that Africa must move beyond policy declarations to the effective implementation of its digital development agenda. He identified connectivity, data governance, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence as priority areas requiring urgent and coordinated action by member states. According to him, Africa must expand access to reliable connectivity, ensure that its data resources deliver value to its people, strengthen collective responses to cyber threats and develop artificial intelligence solutions that reflect African realities and priorities. On the continent’s position in the global technology landscape, George called for a unified African voice in international negotiations on artificial intelligence, data and digital trade. He maintained that Africa’s collective strength, representing nearly 1.5 billion people, must be harnessed to influence global technology standards and policies rather than leaving individual countries to negotiate from weaker positions. “Africa must be at the table, not on the menu,” he stressed, calling for greater continental coordination in shaping the future of the digital economy. The Minister also highlighted Ghana’s One Million Coders Programme as an example of efforts to equip young people with the digital skills needed to participate in the global technology industry. He said Ghana’s leadership would focus on listening to member states, building consensus and driving implementation, insisting that the committee’s performance over the next two years must be judged by tangible outcomes. The chairmanship comes at a critical time as African countries seek to bridge the digital divide, strengthen digital infrastructure, improve data governance and position themselves to benefit from emerging technologies. Ghana’s unanimous confirmation is expected to provide an opportunity for the country to contribute to a more coordinated continental approach to digital development and strengthen Africa’s collective voice in global technology discussions.

items.title: Le ministère enseignement supérieur propose des solutions de substitution pour les médecins exclus de la liste orientée vers l’Algérie pour la spécialisation
items.description: Le ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique a annoncé avoir trouvé des solutions pour les étudiants mauritaniens qui n'ont pas pu s'inscrire dans des programmes de spécialisation médicale en Algérie, en leur permettant d'étudier dans d'autres pays, après que la capacité d'accueil limitée ait empêché leur admission. Le directeur des systèmes d’information au ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique, Sidi Mohamed Ahmed, a déclaré à « Sahara 24 » que le ministère avait orienté des étudiants vers l’Algérie pour y poursuivre leurs études de médecine, mais que les autorités algériennes n’avaient pas pu les inscrire en raison du nombre insuffisant de places disponibles, ce qui a conduit le ministère à leur proposer des alternatives pour qu’ils puissent achever leurs études dans d’autres pays. Cette déclaration fait suite à des plaintes de médecins mauritaniens qui se sont vu écartés des listes des boursiers destinés à suivre une spécialisation médicale en Algérie, bien qu’ils aient accompli toutes les formalités de candidature et que les noms de certains d’entre eux figuraient sur la plateforme électronique dédiée à cet effet. Des médecins, parmi lesquels des diplômés d’universités égyptiennes, ont déclaré avoir été surpris de ne pas trouver leurs noms sur les listes définitives des bénéficiaires de bourses, alors qu’ils avaient fourni tous les documents requis, soulignant que les noms de 12 d’entre eux figuraient sur la plateforme avant d’être écartés des listes ultérieures. Les médecins ont ajouté qu’ils avaient déposé des recours auprès de la direction chargée de l’attribution des bourses et qu’ils s’étaient adressés aux services compétents du ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur, mais qu’ils n’avaient reçu aucune réponse permettant de trancher le sort de leurs demandes ou d’expliquer les raisons pour lesquelles leurs noms n’avaient pas été inclus parmi les bénéficiaires. Le directeur des systèmes d’information n’a pas précisé les pays proposés par le ministère aux étudiants, ni le nombre de personnes concernées par ces solutions alternatives et n’a pas non plus indiqué si ces dispositions englobaient tous les médecins ayant contesté leur exclusion des bourses de spécialisation en Algérie.

items.title: Retro Vibes Day Club donates GH¢20,000 to support breast cancer care in Greater Accra
items.description: Organisers of the Retro Vibes Day Club have donated GH¢20,000 to the Greater Accra Regional Health Directorate to support breast cancer diagnosis, treatment and awareness activities in the region. The donation, presented on behalf of patrons of the monthly social event, is part of the club’s corporate social responsibility efforts to support healthcare delivery and vulnerable people in society. The gesture coincided with Breast Cancer Awareness Month, observed globally in October to promote education, early detection and treatment of the disease. At a brief presentation ceremony in Accra, officials from the Greater Accra Regional Health Directorate commended the group for supporting the region’s breast cancer initiatives and raising awareness of the disease. Dr Louisa Mantey, Metro Director of Health Services, said the contribution would bolster efforts to improve breast cancer education and interventions under the region’s breast cancer campaign. She noted that the support reflected the growing role of community groups and private organisations in complementing government efforts to address public health challenges. Dr Louisa Mantey explained that the Retro Vibes Day Club is a community-based entertainment platform for adults aged 30 and above, bringing people together through music, culture, fashion, and shared experiences. She described the club as a growing community that fostered meaningful relationships and social cohesion while also demonstrating commitment to social causes. “These are young people who understand the health challenges we face as a society and have taken it upon themselves to support the region’s breast cancer drive,” she said. According to the organisers, the donation symbolises the Retro Vibes community’s kindness and generosity, united in support of a cause that affects countless individuals and families. Mr Delanyo Kwashiga, popularly known as DJ Dela and a representative of the organisers, said giving back to society had become a key aspect of the club’s philosophy. “As much as we create opportunities for people to socialise and enjoy themselves, we also believe strongly in supporting worthy causes and making meaningful contributions to communities,” he stated. He explained that the club’s patrons and supporters contributed the GH¢20,000 donation, expressing hope that the initiative would inspire greater public involvement in breast cancer advocacy and healthcare support. DJ Dela said the organisers intended to sustain similar charitable activities and extend support to other health facilities and social intervention programmes. As part of activities marking the October edition of the monthly event, Retro Vibes Day Club partnered with health professionals to provide breast cancer education and screening services for patrons, while encouraging women to undertake regular examinations and seek medical attention for early signs of the disease.

items.title: Ces chantiers de la mort (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Patatras. À Thiès, un immeuble de cinq étages est tombé comme un château de cartes. Les sapeur-pompiers ont mis près de trois heures pour tirer un ouvrier décédé et deux autres blessés des décombres. Et dire que nous sommes passés à quelques mètres de ce chantier la semaine dernière ! Mieux, il y a cinq semaines, dans une de nos vidéos amateurs, on aperçoit ce bâtiment déjà haut de trois niveaux s’élever face à un pan du mur du Stade Lat-Dior. Selon les premières informations, une autorisation de construire pour 3 étages serait finalement « transformée » en 5 étages, malgré les injonctions des autorités compétentes. Les effondrements d’immeubles en chantier, ils font flores à travers le pays ces derniers mois, à Dakar, Rufisque, Touba, etc. Le matériau utilisé est souvent mis en cause, mais le phénomène persiste et la mort d’ouvriers est déplorée à chaque catastrophe. Face aux séries d’accidents meurtriers de voitures sur nos routes, et les récurrents écroulements d’immeubles en chantier, nous peinons à élucider leurs causes, à défaut de les prévenir. Un sursaut national s’impose… omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: 2027: INEC fears poll disruption in insecure areas
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has raised concerns that insecurity could disrupt or prevent the conduct of the 2027 general elections in some parts of the country. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, expressed the concern on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing participants at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections. Amupitan described insecurity in some parts of the country as a major challenge to the conduct of credible elections, calling for urgent and coordinated action by security agencies to protect the electoral process. He said he would engage the National Security Adviser, the Chief of Army Staff and other senior security officials upon his return to Abuja to discuss measures to address the threats and create a safer environment for the elections. The INEC chairman said the commission would adopt a proactive approach to electoral security rather than wait for threats to escalate before responding. He added that INEC was strengthening collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, the Department of State Services, the Armed Forces and other relevant agencies through the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). According to him, the collaboration is designed to improve intelligence-sharing, security coordination and operational preparedness ahead of the 2027 polls. The concerns come as INEC intensifies preparations for the elections, with insecurity posing potential risks to the movement of electoral personnel, distribution of sensitive election materials and participation of voters in affected communities. Amupitan stressed that sustained cooperation between electoral authorities and security agencies would be critical to ensuring that Nigerians could exercise their democratic rights without fear or intimidation. He said early intervention, effective deployment of security personnel and a coordinated response to security threats were necessary to prevent insecurity from undermining the credibility, inclusiveness and peaceful conduct of the 2027 general elections. items.title: EC appointments don’t guarantee electoral victory – Callistus Mahama
items.description: Executive Secretary to President John Dramani Mahama, Callistus Mahama, has argued that appointing the Chairperson of the Electoral Commission (EC) does not guarantee electoral victory for the appointing President or governing party, urging Ghanaians to recognise the decisive role voters play in determining election outcomes. In a commentary on Ghana’s electoral discourse , Mr Mahama said public discussions about EC appointments sometimes appear to undermine confidence in voters’ ability to make independent political choices. “We celebrate the Ghanaian voter as discerning, independent-minded and capable of changing governments. Yet whenever appointments to the Electoral Commission arise, we sometimes speak as though the outcome of the next election has already been negotiated,” he wrote. Mr Mahama cited the 2016 and 2024 general elections as examples of why the political identity of an EC Chairperson should not be treated as a guarantee of victory for the appointing government. In 2015, then-President John Dramani Mahama appointed Charlotte Osei as EC Chairperson. A year later, the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) lost the presidential election to the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo. In 2018, President Akufo-Addo appointed Jean Mensa as EC Chairperson. In the December 2024 elections, the NPP lost power, while John Dramani Mahama won the presidential election and returned to office. “These events should temper the certainty with which some claims about electoral appointments are made,” Mr Mahama wrote. He cautioned, however, that the examples did not establish that electoral administration was free from errors or misconduct, nor did they resolve every concern about individual commissioners. “What they establish is more precise: appointing the chairperson of the Electoral Commission does not guarantee victory for the appointing President or governing party,” he stated. Mr Mahama said explanations of election results that focus almost exclusively on EC appointments risk overlooking the circumstances and considerations that shape voters’ decisions. He pointed to issues such as household incomes, employment opportunities, agricultural production costs, road infrastructure and access to markets as factors that influence citizens’ political choices. “When we explain elections almost entirely through appointments to the Commission, we overlook ordinary people’s political agency. We risk treating citizens as spectators in an exercise whose outcome is supposedly arranged elsewhere,” he wrote. He argued that voters’ experiences and assessments of government performance must remain central to discussions about electoral outcomes. Mr Mahama also stressed that presidential appointments to the EC should not be interpreted as giving the appointing authority control over the Commission’s decisions. He noted that the President appoints members of the Commission on the advice of the Council of State, but said the authority conferred by public office comes with obligations that must be discharged independently. “An appointment confers responsibility, not ownership. A commissioner’s authority comes with obligations defined by public office. The person who makes the appointment does not acquire a claim over how those obligations will be discharged,” he stated. He said the principle applied more broadly to constitutional appointments, arguing that public officials should not be expected to serve the political interests of those who appointed them. Despite his argument that appointments do not guarantee electoral victory, Mr Mahama said scrutiny of the EC and its commissioners remained necessary. He called for impartial electoral administration and improvements in voter registration, polling, collation and dispute resolution. He also urged political actors to support allegations of wrongdoing with evidence and pursue reforms where weaknesses in the electoral process had been demonstrated. “The appointment puts the commissioner in office. The ballot puts the government in office,” he wrote. Mr Mahama’s commentary comes amid debate over the appointment of Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission. The NPP has raised concerns about Madam Agbenyo’s perceived affiliation with the governing NDC and called for her withdrawal. The controversy has renewed debate about the political neutrality of electoral officials and the independence of the Commission. Mr Mahama’s position is that while electoral appointments deserve scrutiny, they should not overshadow the role of voters in determining which party forms the government.

items.title: Apple just announced its first-ever MacBook with a touchscreen
items.description: Apple once scoffed at the idea of a laptop with a touchscreen. But that all changed on Wednesday when the tech giant announced the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, its first laptop with a touch-sensitive display. For years, PC makers have released touchscreen computers to modernise laptops for the mobile era. Apple is late to the game, but is betting its touchscreen laptop will appeal to the MacBook Pro’s core audience of creative professionals and app developers. Today’s announcement is the latest in a blitz of new Apple products launched during John Ternus’ first two months as CEO. The touchscreen MacBook – along with other Apple firsts like the iPhone Duo and HomeView home hub – will test whether Apple can still develop hit products that anticipate users’ needs. Apple’s first touchscreen MacBook The new touchscreen MacBook Pro, which launches on November 6, will come in 14-inch and 16-inch versions and runs on Apple’s M5 Pro or M5 Max chips. The smaller model starts at $2,899, the bigger at $3,399. Apple is touting the touchscreen as being useful for dragging and dropping slides between presentations, allowing developers to directly test on their computers how their apps work. It also highlighted its usefulness for graphic designers and musicians, saying they’ll be able to draw sketches and play virtual instruments with just a touch of the screen. The company also claims many existing apps will work with the touchscreen right away because the software will register touches as clicks. The Dynamic Island, or the pill-shaped cutout at the top of iPhone screens that shows information and the front camera, will also appear on the new laptop. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display also includes additions aimed at creatives, like higher peak brightness than non-touch versions and Adobe’s RGB color space. The company says the touch sensor is built into the display itself rather than layered on top of it, which it claims will reduce latency when swiping and scrolling. Struggles of early touchscreen laptops Touchscreen laptops have existed for more than a decade. Microsoft made a major push to shift the industry in this direction with the release of Windows 8 in 2012. That software featured a new design with larger tile-shaped icons meant to resemble phones and tablets. However, it was widely panned because the operating system was confusing to navigate. The hardware also needed work; early touchscreen laptops were clunky, expensive and awkward to use as tablets. PC makers struggled to keep pace with the rise of smartphones and tablets. “Our competition is different, they’re confused,” Tim Cook, Apple’s then-CEO who is now executive chair of its board of directors, said during a 2013 event . He said rival laptop makers were trying to “make PCs into tablets and tablets into PCs. Who knows what they will do next?” Despite those early gripes, touchscreen laptops have improved over the years thanks to lower component costs, lighter designs, and Windows enhancements. They’re widely available from major PC makers like Dell and Lenovo. Even Apple, which previously criticised hybrid computers, has been inching in its products in this direction for years. It overhauled the iPad’s software in 2019 with more productivity features, like the ability to use more than one app at once. It’s also made its Mac software look more like the iPhone’s by incorporating elements like the control panel for managing settings and the Liquid Glass translucent design for app icons. Yet touchscreen devices only accounted for 16.3% of global laptop shipments in 2025, according to market research from the International Data Corporation. That’s largely because touchscreens aren’t popular with commercial buyers, since most workers plug their laptop into a monitor at their desk, according to Ryan Reith, group vice president at IDC. Apple previously tried to incorporate touch technology into the MacBook Pro in 2016 with the introduction of the Touch Bar, a touch-sensitive strip above the keyboard for accessing app controls and other shortcuts. But consumers largely rejected it because its utility didn’t justify the added cost. Apple’s next era Apple is known for being late to technologies – usually for good reason. It wasn’t the first company to launch MP3 players, tablets, or smartwatches, but it made those products popular by making its devices simpler and easier to use. The touchscreen MacBook Pro is the latest in a series of recent examples following this playbook. The company introduced its HomeView smart home hub earlier this month, attempting to challenge Amazon’s dominance in the smart home industry. And last week, Apple’s first foldable iPhone went on sale, debuting long after chief rival Samsung established a lead in that market. Apple has long faced pressure to deliver new blockbuster products, especially given Ternus’s hardware background compared with Cook’s operations expertise. Wall Street will watch how Apple’s new products are received on the company’s earnings call next week, especially after reports of broken iPhone Duo screens . Still, some analysts think Apple’s new laptop will raise the bar for Windows rivals. “Apple’s entry will not dramatically change the PC market, but it will change the status of touch-enabled laptops,” Francisco Jeronimo, an analyst covering mobile devices and computers, said in an email following Apple’s announcement.

items.title: El BCE deja sin cambios los tipos y apunta a un freno en el crecimiento
items.description: La sorpresa del Consejo de Gobierno que ha celebrado hoy el BCE no ha venido por su decisión sobre política monetaria, sino por el anuncio de Christine Lagarde de dejar la presidencia de la institución el próximo 7 de febrero . El BCE ha decidido mantener sin cambios los tipos de interés en el 2,5%, hacer una pausa después de la subida adoptada en septiembre , un impasse sin anuncios de calado que la presidenta ha aprovechado para comunicar su salida anticipada. Pero la calma es solo aparente en la autoridad monetaria de la zona euro. No solo por el intenso proceso que comienza para la renovación de su cúpula sino por las tareas urgentes que siguen ahí: la amenaza inflacionista, que no cesa con las guerras en Irán y Ucrania encareciendo la energía, y la tensión sobre la deuda soberana francesa, que ha llevado a su prima de riesgo a niveles no vistos desde 2011. El avance del PIB surge además como motivo de preocupación y, en un tono más suave que en otras ocasiones, el BCE apunta que el efecto de las dos alzas de tipos ya decididas este año “probablemente afectará al crecimiento”. items.title: Ato Forson to present 2027 Budget on Nov. 12 as jobs take centre stage
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson will present the 2027 Budget to Parliament on November 12, Deputy Finance Minister Thomas Nyarko Ampem has announced. Mr Ampem confirmed the date at the release of the Ghana Statistical Service’s Ghana in Numbers report in Accra. He said the budget would also outline the government’s New Economy agenda. The Deputy Minister described the report’s release as timely as preparations for the budget presentation continued. He urged the Ghana Statistical Service to give every Member of Parliament access to its dashboard to support informed debate in the House. Mr Ampem also said the report would strengthen transparency in economic data and help guide planning and policy decisions. Areas of Focus Job creation, economic transformation and growth-focused spending are expected to feature prominently in the budget as the government seeks to consolidate recent economic gains. JoyBusiness understands from sources familiar with the preparations that Dr Forson is likely to outline measures to move Ghana beyond stabilisation towards sustained growth and employment. The proposed theme is “New Economy, New Ghana: Jobs and Prosperity”, although this has yet to be confirmed. The policy direction is expected to prioritise local value addition to boost production, export earnings and jobs. Sources indicate that the budget could include significant allocations to complete ongoing infrastructure projects. However, overall spending is not expected to depart substantially from the estimates outlined in the 2026 Budget. Planned expenditure is expected to remain within the government’s fiscal and debt framework, with an emphasis on avoiding excessive deficits and spending overruns. Dr Forson may also outline plans to lower the primary surplus target to create additional room for priority spending. Sources say the government sees this approach as the next phase of economic policy following the current fiscal adjustment programme. The budget could target economic growth of about 5% in 2027 and inflation of 8%, with a two-percentage-point tolerance band. The medium-term strategy is expected to preserve fiscal and debt sustainability while creating space for investments that support economic transformation. Sources say the measures will also seek to safeguard macroeconomic stability, strengthen resilience and protect poor and vulnerable households. The New Economy Programme The New Economy Programme is expected to be central to the budget, with a greater emphasis on growth-focused spending alongside continued fiscal discipline. Sources say the government intends to use the programme to expand economic opportunities and support employment. Dr Forson is also expected to stress the need for continued discipline and commitment to sustain recent gains. Priority areas identified in the New Economy blueprint include: Macroeconomic stability; Commercial agriculture, agro-industry and agribusiness; Energy sector reforms and investment; Critical minerals and value addition; Cotton, textiles and garments; and Tourism, culture and the creative arts.

items.title: Callistus Mahama urges parties to focus on voters rather than EC appointments
items.description: Executive Secretary to President John Dramani Mahama, Callistus Mahama, said political parties must focus on persuading voters and strengthening their election-day operations rather than allowing suspicions about the political affiliations of Electoral Commission (EC) officials to dominate electoral debates. He argued that concerns about the composition of the Commission should not distract parties from the work of building public confidence, developing credible policies and maintaining relationships with voters. “Winning votes requires organisation, credible leadership, persuasive policies and attention to the concerns of communities. Retaining those votes requires performance and a continuing relationship with citizens,” he wrote in a commentary on Ghana’s electoral discourse. “Suspicion about the Electoral Commission cannot substitute for this work.” Warning against complacency Mr Mahama cautioned that portraying electoral victory as dependent primarily on who occupies positions at the Commission could encourage complacency among supporters when they favour an appointment and fatalism when they oppose it. “There is little democratic value in teaching supporters that victory depends principally on who occupies an office at the Commission. Such a message can encourage complacency when a party feels comfortable with an appointment and fatalism when it does not,” he stated. He urged political leaders to promote lawful vigilance while encouraging supporters to engage in active campaigning and voter mobilisation. “Supporters should understand both the importance of protecting their votes and the need to persuade others to vote with them,” he wrote. Parties urged to strengthen polling station operations Mr Mahama also challenged political parties to translate their emphasis on polling stations into practical preparations for election day. While acknowledging the importance of protecting votes, he said parties needed to ensure their agents were adequately prepared to monitor proceedings, verify figures, maintain records and promptly report discrepancies. “Agents must understand their responsibilities. They must observe, check figures, keep relevant records, and report discrepancies promptly. Parties must organise credible systems for tracking results and following collation,” he said. He warned that parties risked neglecting essential electoral responsibilities when they devoted significant attention to public commentary without investing adequately in these operational tasks. Calls for evidence-based electoral debate Mr Mahama advocated a more substantive national conversation about electoral integrity, centred on whether eligible citizens could register and vote, election procedures were applied consistently, and officials were adequately prepared. He also highlighted the importance of transparent result verification, open correction of errors and credible mechanisms for resolving electoral disputes. “The volume of debate is less important than its quality. A loud accusation may reveal little. A carefully documented discrepancy may reveal a great deal,” he said. He argued that scrutiny should focus on verifiable evidence and procedures capable of improving the electoral process rather than on political suspicion alone. Calls for consistent standards Mr Mahama further urged political actors to apply the same standards to electoral appointments and institutional decisions, regardless of which party holds power. He posed questions about whether parties would defend the same appointment procedures under a different government or accept explanations from officials they distrusted. He said such questions could expose instances in which arguments about institutional independence were shaped by immediate political interests rather than consistent democratic principles. Background to the debate Mr Mahama’s commentary comes amid debate over the appointment of Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah and Emelia Afi Agbenyo as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission. The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has raised concerns about Madam Agbenyo’s perceived affiliation with the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) and called for her withdrawal. The controversy has renewed discussion about the political neutrality of electoral officials and the standards that should guide appointments to the Commission. Mr Mahama’s intervention argues that, alongside scrutiny of appointments, political parties must invest in voter persuasion, election monitoring and evidence-based challenges to any irregularities.

items.title: EU hits pause on country-level social media bans for children
items.description: The European Union (EU) said on Thursday it does not want any more national-level bans on social media before a pan-European law is approved, as it blocked draft rules put forward by Austria. Under EU law, member states must notify the European Commission to ensure their bills do not break the bloc’s rules. Austria wanted to ban children under 14 from social media, but the EU said no. “The commission has decided to postpone for 12 months any draft national laws overlapping with the future harmonised rules,” EU spokesman Thomas Regnier said. The European Commission last month proposed to ban children under 13 from social media, and permit only limited, supervised access until the age of 15. The EU believes allowing countries to move ahead with national laws would divide the bloc, creating varying age-limits among member states. Brussels also fears EU countries will not rush to pass the bloc-wide law if they have their own country-level rules in place. “We need to now focus on the negotiations of the EU Kids Act and to ensure an effective enforcement of our rules,” Regnier said. The commission hopes EU countries and the European Parliament will reach a deal on the new rules in the next few months. There will, however, be exceptions to the EU’s decision. Although the commission demanded France’s proposed law be reworked, it is not expected to be blocked because Paris notified Brussels of the law before bloc-wide legislation was put forward. And Greece has been able to pass its own rules, drafted long before September. Regnier would not be drawn on whether France would be prevented from enacting its national legislation. The EU has yet to deliver verdicts on bans by other EU states, including Italy and Slovakia.

items.title: Russian aluminium giant Rusal plans to mine bauxite in Ghana
items.description: Russian aluminium giant Rusal is considering a joint venture in Ghana to mine and process bauxite, the raw material used to produce aluminium, Russia’s state news agency RIA has reported, citing a memorandum signed on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The Chief Executive Officer, Evgeny Nikitin, told RIA that the company was targeting an annual bauxite production of 5.0 million metric tons in Ghana and a processing capacity of 1.2 million metric tons per year. The agreement was signed with Ghana Integrated Aluminium Development Corporation (GIADEC) on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum in Moscow. The agreement will mark Rusal’s first venture in Ghana beyond its established operations in Guinea. Rusal, the world’s largest aluminium producer outside China, already has major bauxite operations in Guinea, where it owns and operates Compagnie des Bauxites de Kindia (CBK), develops the Dian-Dian deposit and runs the Friguia complex. It operates seven bauxite mines worldwide, including two in Russia. The company produced 18.453 million metric tons of bauxite in 2025, with captive production covering 88% of its alumina refineries’ requirements. Rusal’s move aligns with Ghana’s ambitions to boost domestic value‑addition in its bauxite sector. Nyinahin in the Ashanti region has the largest deposit in the country with an estimated 700 million metric tonnes. Awaso, the oldest and currently active mining area in the Western region holds 60 million metric tonnes of reserves. Ghana holds approximately 900 million metric tons of bauxite reserves—the seventh largest globally.

items.title: L’amour à l’épreuve du sang (par Souleymane Diam SY)
items.description: La question mérite d’être posée, avec gravité. Jusqu’à quand faudra-t-il compter les victimes avant que la société ne prenne la mesure de cette hécatombe ? Le constat est glaçant, la réponse déconcertante. Les violences et les meurtres impliquant des conjoints ou des petits amis se succèdent à un rythme alarmant. La peur s’installe là où devraient régner l’amour, la confiance et la sécurité. Ce qui devrait être un espace d’affection devient, pour certaines femmes, un piège mortel. Derrière chaque drame, une vie fauchée, une famille brisée et une société confrontée à son impuissance. Après l’agression à l’acide contre Astou Pierre, dont le présumé auteur, son petit ami, a fui au Maroc il y a quelques semaines, deux autres affaires sont venues alourdir ce sinistre tableau, à Podor et à Thiès. À Podor, la lycéenne A. Sy a été froidement tuée, placée dans un sac et abandonnée. Son petit ami, principal suspect, reste introuvable depuis la découverte macabre qui a plongé la ville dans l’émoi. Élève en classe de Terminale, cette jeune fille avait un avenir et des espoirs qui ont été brutalement anéantis. À Thiès, dans le quartier de Keur Massamba Guèye, un autre drame s’est produit dans la nuit du samedi 24 au dimanche 25 octobre 2026. Vers 22 heures, une jeune femme de 25 ans a été mortellement poignardée au domicile de son petit ami, M. Sy, âgé de 42 ans. Selon les premiers éléments, elle s’y était rendue pour récupérer son téléphone, que ce dernier lui aurait dérobé. Une dispute a alors dégénéré. Grièvement blessé au cours des faits, le mis en cause a été évacué à l’hôpital régional de Thiès avant d’être interpellé et placé en garde à vue. Deux drames, deux femmes tuées et la même interrogation lancinante : comment en arrive-t-on à considérer la vie d’une femme comme une chose dont on pourrait disposer à sa guise ? Les scénarios se répètent avec une régularité effrayante. Derrière ces tragédies se dessine souvent le même mécanisme : le refus de la rupture, la volonté de contrôler l’autre et cette prétention à faire de l’amour un droit de propriété. Pour certains, la séparation n’est pas un choix à respecter, mais une offense à punir. La femme qui part devient une cible, comme si sa liberté constituait une provocation. La logique est brutale et inacceptable : « Si tu n’es plus à moi, tu ne seras à personne. » Au nom d’une blessure d’orgueil, certains basculent dans la violence extrême, jusqu’à ôter la vie à celle qu’ils prétendaient aimer. Disons-le sans détour : la jalousie n’est pas une preuve d’amour, la possession n’est pas un engagement et la violence n’est jamais une réponse à la rupture. Aucun chagrin, aucune frustration, aucune humiliation ne justifie un meurtre. Certes, le cœur a ses raisons que la raison ignore. Mais cette formule ne doit pas servir d’excuse à l’aveuglement. La confiance est indispensable, mais elle ne doit jamais conduire à fermer les yeux sur l’inacceptable. Une relation ne doit exiger ni soumission, ni peur, ni sacrifice de sa liberté. Être vigilant, ce n’est pas vivre dans une méfiance permanente. C’est savoir reconnaître les comportements inquiétants et refuser de les justifier au nom des sentiments. Jalousie excessive, contrôle des déplacements et des fréquentations, surveillance du téléphone, harcèlement, menaces en cas de séparation, violences verbales ou psychologiques sont autant de signaux à prendre au sérieux. Il ne s’agit pas de condamner sans preuve, mais de ne pas attendre qu’une femme soit gravement blessée ou tuée pour reconnaître qu’elle était en danger. La récurrence de ces drames impose de regarder la réalité en face. Lorsque des femmes sont tuées par leur conjoint ou leur partenaire, ou en raison de violences liées à leur condition de femme, le terme de féminicide doit pouvoir être employé lorsque les faits le justifient. Nommer ces crimes, c’est les rendre visibles, mieux les documenter et rappeler qu’il ne s’agit pas de simples différends privés, mais d’un enjeu majeur de sécurité et de protection. Une femme ne doit pas avoir à choisir entre sa liberté et sa vie. Elle doit pouvoir aimer sans trembler, se séparer sans être menacée et dénoncer les violences sans craindre de ne pas être entendue. Car, il est temps de comprendre que l’amour ne donne aucun droit sur la vie d’autrui. Lorsqu’une femme paie de sa vie le prix de sa liberté, ce n’est pas seulement un drame individuel. C’est toute la société qui échoue à protéger l’une des libertés les plus fondamentales : celle de vivre, de choisir et de partir. souleymanediam.sy@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Erfoud accueille la 15ᵉ édition du SIDATTES sur fond de récolte record
items.description: La 15e édition du Salon international des dattes au Maroc (SIDATTES) a ouvert ses portes mercredi 28 octobre à Erfoud, sous le signe de l’innovation et du développement des territoires oasiens. La production nationale de dattes devrait atteindre près de 177.000 tonnes au titre de la campagne agricole 2026-2027, soit une progression de 11 % par rapport à la saison précédente. Le Maroc s’attend à enregistrer une production record de dattes pour la campagne agricole 2026-2027. Selon les prévisions présentées à l’occasion de la 15e édition du Salon international des dattes au Maroc (SIDATTES), organisée à Erfoud, le volume national devrait avoisiner les 177.000 tonnes, en hausse de 11 % par rapport à la campagne précédente. Ouvert mercredi 28 octobre sous le Haut Patronage du Roi Mohammed VI, le salon se tient cette année autour du thème « Palmier dattier et innovation : opportunités pour le développement territorial intégré » . La cérémonie d’inauguration a été présidée par le ministre de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche maritime et de la Souveraineté alimentaire, Khalid Hatimy, en présence de plusieurs responsables gouvernementaux, d’élus, de professionnels du secteur agricole et de représentants d’institutions partenaires. Organisé par l’Association du Salon international des dattes au Maroc (ASIDMA), avec l’appui de l’Agence nationale pour le développement des zones oasiennes et de l’arganier (ANDZOA), le SIDATTES constitue un rendez-vous majeur pour les professionnels de la filière phoenicicole. Il vise à favoriser les échanges, les partenariats et la commercialisation des produits, tout en soutenant la valorisation de l’agriculture oasienne et le développement économique régional. Plus de 200 exposants réunis à Erfoud Déployée sur une superficie de 40.000 m², cette édition réunit plus de 200 exposants marocains et étrangers et devrait accueillir plus de 100.000 visiteurs. Le salon s’articule autour de huit pôles thématiques consacrés notamment aux régions productrices, aux institutions et sponsors, aux participations internationales, aux intrants agricoles, au machinisme, à la Rahba, aux produits du terroir et à l’élevage. L’innovation occupe une place centrale dans cette édition. Les organisateurs mettent en avant les solutions susceptibles de moderniser les pratiques agricoles, d’améliorer la gestion des ressources naturelles et de renforcer la valorisation des dattes. L’objectif est d’accroître la compétitivité de la filière tout en préservant les écosystèmes oasiens, particulièrement exposés aux contraintes climatiques et hydriques. La filière des dattes représente un levier économique et social important pour les territoires oasiens. Elle génère une valeur ajoutée de plus de 3 milliards de dirhams, assure plus de 3,4 millions de journées de travail par an et peut représenter jusqu’à 60 % du revenu agricole des ménages oasiens. Près de 2 millions de Marocains en tireraient des revenus, directement ou indirectement. Au-delà de son poids économique, cette activité contribue à la limitation de l’exode rural, à la lutte contre la désertification et à la préservation du patrimoine oasien. Elle s’inscrit dans la continuité des politiques agricoles engagées dans le cadre du Plan Maroc Vert, puis de la stratégie Génération Green 2020-2030. La hausse attendue de la production nationale s’expliquerait notamment par l’amélioration des conditions climatiques et l’entrée en production de nouvelles superficies plantées dans les zones d’extension. La région de Drâa-Tafilalet demeure le principal bassin phoenicicole du Royaume, avec 83 % de la production nationale. Les régions de Souss-Massa et de l’Oriental contribuent chacune à hauteur de 7,5 %. Dans Drâa-Tafilalet, les oasis s’étendent sur près de 56.000 hectares et comptent plus de 6,49 millions de palmiers dattiers. Elles abritent une diversité de plus de 225 variétés de dattes. Les exportations régionales ont atteint 1.510 tonnes en 2026. Recherche et innovation pour préserver les oasis En marge de l’ouverture du salon, le ministre de l’Agriculture a effectué une visite de terrain dans la province d’Errachidia, consacrée à la recherche agronomique, à la gestion durable des écosystèmes oasiens et à la modernisation des infrastructures hydroagricoles. La visite a débuté au Laboratoire national de culture in vitro du palmier dattier, relevant du Centre régional de la recherche agronomique d’Errachidia de l’Institut national de la recherche agronomique (INRA). Cette structure joue un rôle dans la multiplication du palmier dattier et la régénération des oasis marocaines. Ses activités portent notamment sur la production de plants sélectionnés présentant une qualité génétique élevée, la préservation des ressources génétiques nationales et le développement des techniques de culture in vitro. Le laboratoire contribue également aux efforts de lutte contre la maladie du Bayoud grâce à la multiplication de génotypes sélectionnés. Le ministre s’est ensuite rendu à Ouled Chaker, dans la commune d’Aoufous, pour s’informer sur le Projet de gestion durable des écosystèmes oasiens (PROGEDOM), mis en œuvre par l’ANDZOA avec l’appui du Groupe de la Banque mondiale. Prévu de septembre 2024 à décembre 2027, ce projet mobilise une enveloppe de 164 millions de dirhams, dont 121 millions sous forme de don du fonds PROGREEN de la Banque mondiale et 43 millions au titre de la contribution du ministère de l’Agriculture. Il cible environ 37.000 habitants des oasis d’Aoufous, dans la province d’Errachidia, et d’Akka, dans la province de Tata. Le programme vise à renforcer la résilience des écosystèmes oasiens face aux changements climatiques et à favoriser la mobilisation des ressources en eau. À cette occasion, une opération de distribution d’équipements agricoles destinés au nettoyage des oasis et à la valorisation des sous-produits du palmier dattier a également été supervisée. Près de 180 millions de dirhams de travaux hydroagricoles Au ksar El Maâdid, dans la commune territoriale d’Arab Sebbah, le ministre a pris connaissance de l’avancement du projet d’aménagement hydroagricole du périmètre du grand hydraulique de l’Oued Ziz et de la plaine du Tafilalet. Ce projet couvre environ 28.000 hectares, répartis sur 540 ksour, et bénéficie à près de 114.800 habitants. Les travaux réalisés depuis 2020 représentent un montant d’environ 179,94 millions de dirhams. En marge du salon, des vitroplants de palmier dattier ont également été distribués à des petits agriculteurs dans le cadre du programme d’intensification et de réhabilitation des oasis traditionnelles de Drâa-Tafilalet. Doté d’une enveloppe de 792 millions de dirhams pour la période 2021-2030, ce programme couvre quatre provinces et 58 communes territoriales. À ce jour, 917.051 plants ont été distribués, sur un objectif total de 2,6 millions. Renforcer la compétitivité de la filière Le ministre a par ailleurs tenu une réunion avec la Fédération interprofessionnelle des dattes afin d’examiner les perspectives de développement de la filière phoenicicole. Les échanges ont porté sur la poursuite de l’accompagnement des professionnels, le renforcement de la compétitivité et de la résilience du secteur, ainsi que la préservation du patrimoine oasien. Avec une production prévisionnelle de 177.000 tonnes, le Maroc aborde la campagne 2026-2027 avec des perspectives favorables. Le défi reste désormais de consolider cette dynamique dans la durée, en modernisant les pratiques agricoles, en valorisant les variétés nationales et en protégeant les ressources naturelles dont dépend l’avenir des oasis.
