items.title: 'Not related to defence': Govt responds to Fazl's remarks about Makkah pact countries' meeting in Tehran
items.description: Federal ministers on Thursday responded to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s remarks regarding a recent huddle in Tehran comprising the Makkah defence pact countries and Iran. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said the meeting was not related to defence. Hence, Asif said his presence was not required, while Naqvi explained the reasons for his participation. The remarks came after the JUI-F chief questioned Asif’s absence and Naqvi’s presence at the meeting. The meeting brought together top officials from Iran and member countries of the Makkah Defence Alliance — including Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin. On Iran’s side, President Masoud Pezeshkian, Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi were present. The huddle agreed to “continue their dialogue to bolster cooperation among the four regional nations, including in the areas of regional peace and security”. On Wednesday, Fazl referred to the development during his address in the National Assembly (NA) and commented: “A defence pact is taking shape in Iran, a meeting is under way (there), and the defence minister is sitting here.” Amid laughter and desk thumping in the Lower House, he referred to Naqvi’s presence at the Tehran huddle and questioned: “The interior minister is required there as well?” Then, taking a jibe at Asif, he repeated the defence minister’s phrase that he had used against the PTI. “There is your respect and stature — koi sharam hoti hai, koi haya hoti hai (have some shame, show some modesty),” he said, breaking into laughter. Responding to him in the NA on Thursday, Asif said no defence pact was taking shape in Tehran, nor was the discussion focused on Pakistan’s defence or any related matter. He said CDF Munir had “assumed a role for Pakistan” following last year’s military conflict with India. That role, he said, was of “peace and dialogue so that peace is established in our region”. Since then, he noted, Pakistan has signed two defence pacts — the Makkah defence pact and the Badr Memorandum of Understanding. “I was involved in those pacts as I am the defence minister,” he explained, adding that the meeting in Tehran was “not the defence ministry’s mandate”. The CDF had gone there “as a messenger of peace and paved the ground” for the huddle, he said, ostensibly referring to Tehran last week. During that visit, the CDF had proposed the Tehran meeting, according to Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei. Asif said this was the situation and he was “not needed in Tehran”. He added that the CDF had played a role in averting a confrontation. “The situation could have deteriorated as far as the Yemen issue is concerned […] There has been some talk and peace may emerge in the coming days or week as far as Saudi Arabia versus Yemen [sic] is concerned.” Asif advised Fazl to be the bigger person and said his criticism was “misplaced”. The defence minister further said Pakistan’s and the CDF’s role at the international level should be acknowledged, keeping political differences aside. He said one should at least show some dignity. ‘Not related to defence’ Meanwhile, in the Senate, Naqvi also responded to Fazl’s remarks on his participation in the Tehran meeting. The proceedings were marred by loud exchanges between the interior minister and JUI-F Senator Kamran Murtaza. Naqvi clarified that he and CDF Munir undertook the visit to “handle the ongoing crisis in Iran”. On Fazl’s query of why Asif had not gone there, he said, “He (Fazl) did not know that this [trip] was not related to defence.” Defending his inclusion, the minister said: “I do not go out of my own volition. I have been especially tasked by the prime minister sahib ; he has entrusted me with some matters regarding the current crisis of the [Iran] war, because of which I go.” Naqvi said he wanted to ask Fazl and his party’s senators present there just one question and then noted that JUI-F leaders had made very “disgusting statements about institutions” three to four months ago. This seemingly prompted Senator Murtaza to object, and the presiding officer immediately said he was expunging the word “disgusting” from Naqvi’s remarks. As Murtaza continued shouting, Naqvi said, “You should listen here … You will have to listen.” The presiding officer noted that Naqvi was a member of the Senate and urged the JUI-F leader to take his seat. Resuming his remarks, Naqvi said, “Giving people the perception that this was a defence pact; this was not a defence agreement at all. The independent senator added: “For them, the state is like a mother until the day they can squeeze it dry. The state is very good as long as they can extract wealth from the state, and when you do not get a share in the state and the government, then you spit on the state. This is not appropriate anywhere.” Murtaza again interrupted, objecting to Naqvi’s language, at which the latter replied that the other side had also used similar language a day ago. As the JUI-F senator continued speaking amid the presiding officer’s calls to halt cross-talk, Naqvi said, “If they criticise, they should garner and keep the courage to take the answer as well. This is no way [to behave] that you go and say whatever you want.” The interior minister then went on to criticise the JUI-F, alleging that it “used Islam for business and for politics”. Amid the ruckus, PML-N’s Abid Sher Ali also stood up and responded loudly, prompting State Minister of Interior Tallal Chaudhry and the presiding officer to urge him to take his seat. Naqvi then addressed PTI’s Ali Zafar and said, “These very people (JUI-F) used to come to us before governor’s rule [was imposed] and say, ‘Impose governor’s rule, rid us of them!’ […] Those who come and sit with you and engage in opposition wanted governor’s rule imposed from their hearts. I will prove this to you.” Addressing JUI-F, the interior minister said, “Now, you will not get jobs in the state. Now you will not get money from the state, nor will you get tickets from the state.” He asserted that it was the JUI-F that was “continuously crossing the line” and that they would get a response if they kept doing so. ‘Full of contradictions’ In his remarks in the NA, Asif alleged that Fazl’s past “is full of contradictions”. “You taunt me with ‘have some shame, show some modesty’, but you should also have some shame and show some modesty. How many perks have you enjoyed over the past 40 years? You have been violating the very principles that you have been highlighting,” Asif said. He recalled that Fazl had also offered to mediate with Kabul. “Were you the foreign minister?” he questioned, alleging that the move was aimed at “value addition to his politics and leverage that to extract maximum advantage from the government”. Asif said Fazl had been in the government with every political party, making an incomplete remark: “When you don’t get a share in the power —” “When you delete the past from your memory and attack your rivals — at least I don’t have that courage. When I speak, my past is fresh in my mind; that if I say this, whether I would be taunted that we supported General Ziaul Haq’s government,” he went on to say. The defence minister recalled that Fazl was part of the Musharraf government, had also been an opposition leader in the House and also served as the Kashmir Committee chairperson. He said a person serving as the head of such a committee that raises issues at an international forum should have “impeccable credentials”. When some lawmakers opposed him in favour of Fazl, he remarked, “The Maulana now needs women’s support. He is unable to find a man.” He also accused Fazl of “targeting our diplomatic efforts”, saying that the government’s achievement at the global stage had not received the commendation they deserved. Asif said his advice to the JUI-F would be a line often seen on buses and trucks: “ Mehnat kar, hasad na kar (work hard and don’t envy).” He ended his address, alleging that had Fazl been given some share in the governance in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the JUI-F chief’s address the previous day would not have been delivered. “This sideshow that they (JUI-F) are running, I feel that it is unfortunate that our sisters have been forced to defend the men [of JUI-F] while the men are nowhere to be seen,” Asif remarked. Describing Fazl’s address as “blackmail”, Asif warned against coming into power based on “compromises”. “Sitting in the opposition would be a more respectable approach, rather than sitting with people who will blackmail you,” he said. “We as senior parliamentarians should convey to the nation that we will not do group-based politics but politics rooted in the constitution and [..] for the security of the country,” Asif urged, adding that lawmakers should chart a way forward together, rather than “grabbing each other by the collar”.

items.title: The ballot is mightier than the appointment – Reflections on EC, political suspicion and the sovereignty of the Ghanaian voter
items.description: A contradiction lies at the heart of our electoral conversation. We celebrate the Ghanaian voter as discerning, independent-minded and capable of changing governments. Yet whenever appointments to the Electoral Commission arise, we sometimes speak as though the outcome of the next election has already been negotiated. Suddenly, attention shifts from the millions who will cast their ballots to the handful entrusted with administering the process. The appointing President is presumed to have secured an advantage. The appointee is assigned a political identity. And the voter, whose judgment should occupy the centre of the discussion, is pushed towards its margins. This tendency deserves reflection. Public concern about the Electoral Commission is understandable. Elections determine who exercises public power, and those who administer them carry an exceptional responsibility. Citizens are entitled to demand competence, integrity and impartiality from every commissioner. But vigilance can become habitual suspicion, and political argument can exaggerate the power of the very institution it claims to scrutinise. The Electoral Commission has an indispensable role in our democracy. It does not possess the electorate’s power to choose a government. Two elections offer a useful starting point. In 2015, President John Dramani Mahama appointed Charlotte Osei as Chairperson of the Electoral Commission. In December 2016, Mahama lost the presidential election. The Commission she chaired declared Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo the winner. In 2018, President Akufo-Addo appointed Jean Mensa as Chairperson. In December 2024, the governing New Patriotic Party lost the presidential election under her leadership. John Dramani Mahama won and returned to the presidency. These events should temper the certainty with which some claims about electoral appointments are made. They do not establish that electoral administration is immune from error or misconduct. They also do not settle every concern that may arise about a particular commissioner. What they establish is more precise: appointing the chairperson of the Electoral Commission does not guarantee victory for the appointing President or governing party. That lesson applies equally to the NDC and the NPP. Indeed, the strength of these examples lies in their symmetry. Each major party has experienced defeat under a Commission chaired by a person appointed by its own government. Each therefore has reason to approach the subject with greater humility. Our electoral history should help us refine our arguments. It should prevent us from repeatedly presenting as inevitable what experience has already shown to be uncertain. Behind every election result are citizens weighing the circumstances of their lives. A trader considers whether sales can sustain the household. A young graduate reflects on employment prospects. A farmer thinks about production costs, roads and access to markets. A parent weighs school expenses. A pensioner considers the purchasing power of an income that must stretch further each month. Others vote from conviction, party loyalty, confidence in a candidate, approval of government performance or a desire for change. Many weigh several considerations at once. These judgments cannot be reduced to the identity of an electoral commissioner. When we explain elections almost entirely through appointments to the Commission, we overlook ordinary people’s political agency. We risk treating citizens as spectators in an exercise whose outcome is supposedly arranged elsewhere. That is a poor account of democracy. The voter may listen quietly while politicians argue loudly. Silence should never be mistaken for the absence of judgment. The eventual ballot may contain a verdict that no rally, radio discussion or confident prediction fully anticipated. Political parties should take that independence seriously. An appointment confers responsibility, not ownership Ghana’s Constitution allows the President to appoint members of the Electoral Commission on the advice of the Council of State. It also protects the Commission from external direction or control in performing its functions, subject to the Constitution and consistent laws. Appointment and operational independence are therefore intended to coexist. The distinction is fundamental. A commissioner’s authority comes with obligations defined by public office. The person who makes the appointment does not acquire a claim over how those obligations will be discharged. This principle reaches beyond the Electoral Commission. A constitutional system could scarcely function if every public appointment were understood as a permanent instruction to serve the political interests of the appointing authority. The transition into independent office must carry meaning. It requires judgment, restraint and the willingness to act lawfully even when doing so disappoints those who welcomed the appointment. At the same time, a lawful appointment process does not make every appointment beyond question. Citizens may reasonably examine a nominee’s professional record, conduct, associations and potential conflicts of interest. Where credible evidence shows active partisanship or conduct incompatible with impartial administration, it deserves serious attention. But the argument must identify that evidence. The name of the appointing President cannot, by itself, carry the entire case. What the Commission actually does The Electoral Commission’s constitutional responsibilities include compiling and revising the voters’ register, demarcating electoral boundaries, conducting public elections and referenda, and educating citizens about the electoral process. These are substantial responsibilities. Decisions about registration, access, logistics and electoral procedures can affect whether citizens participate effectively and whether contestants compete fairly. It would therefore be mistaken to suggest that the Commission is merely a ceremonial body that appears at the end of an election to announce figures. Its administrative work matters before, during and after polling. A credible election depends on much more than an accurate announcement on declaration day. Nevertheless, the purpose of all that work is to give effect to choices made by citizens. The Commission must provide a fair process, safeguard its integrity and declare the lawful outcome. Its authority does not include a preference about who should govern. The more clearly we understand this mandate, the more intelligently we can scrutinise its performance. The meaning of the polling station The statement that “elections are won at the polling stations” is often repeated. It deserves to be understood beyond its usefulness as a political slogan. The polling station is where the citizen’s choice enters the official record. It is where actual votes must eventually support broad claims of popularity. Ghana’s constitutional framework requires counting votes at polling stations in the presence of candidates, their representatives, or polling agents. It provides for recording, signing, and announcing polling-station results. These arrangements give the process a local, observable foundation. This has practical implications for political parties. Agents must understand their responsibilities. They must observe, check figures, keep relevant records, and report discrepancies promptly. Parties must organise credible systems for tracking results and following collation. A party that invests heavily in public commentary while neglecting these tasks leaves essential work undone. Yet the polling-station argument must also be carried through to its logical conclusion. A correctly counted vote must remain correctly recorded as results move through collation and declaration. Transparency must extend across the whole process. An election is credible when the declared outcome can be traced back to the underlying votes through records that withstand scrutiny. Confidence should grow from that capacity to verify. Political parties must return to the work of persuasion The fixation on commissioners can distract from a more demanding political task: earning the confidence of the electorate. Winning votes requires organisation, credible leadership, persuasive policies and attention to the concerns of communities. Retaining those votes requires performance and a continuing relationship with citizens. Suspicion about the Electoral Commission cannot substitute for this work. A governing party must ask whether it has met expectations. An opposition party must explain why it deserves to be entrusted with power. Both must listen closely enough to hear what citizens are actually saying. There is little democratic value in teaching supporters that victory depends principally on who occupies an office at the Commission. Such a message can encourage complacency when a party feels comfortable with an appointment and fatalism when it does not. Neither attitude helps citizens participate confidently. Political leadership should encourage lawful vigilance alongside purposeful campaigning. Supporters should understand both the importance of protecting their votes and the need to persuade others to vote with them. The same standard in government and opposition Perhaps the most revealing test of principle is whether it survives a change in political circumstances. Would we defend the same appointment procedure if another party controlled the presidency? Would we accept the same explanation from a commissioner we distrusted? Would evidence sufficient for an accusation against an opponent also be sufficient against someone we support? These questions are uncomfortable because they expose how easily institutional arguments can become instruments of immediate political convenience. If a party believes the appointment framework requires reform, it should advocate a model it would accept under any government. It should explain how that model improves competence, independence, transparency and accountability. Reform deserves a serious national conversation. It should be pursued with a view to the next generation of elections, rather than only the next electoral contest. Institutions become stronger when political actors can agree on rules whose legitimacy does not depend on who benefits first. The Commission also carries a continuing responsibility to earn public confidence. Independence does not remove the need to explain decisions. Indeed, an institution entrusted with such consequential duties should understand the value of clear reasons, timely information and respectful engagement. When an error occurs, correction should be prompt and transparent. When a procedure is disputed, the applicable rule should be explained. When stakeholders raise a credible concern, the response should address its substance. Commissioners must also exercise care in their public conduct. Their words reach an audience that includes competing parties and citizens with sharply different loyalties. Professional restraint helps keep attention on the institution’s work. Trust cannot rest entirely on appeals to the character of those in office. It needs dependable procedures, accessible information, and consistent conduct. The ideal is an electoral system in which citizens can assess what happened without first deciding whose personality they trust. A better debate, rather than simply a quieter one Comparisons with other democracies should be made carefully. Countries organise electoral administration through different arrangements, including independent, governmental and mixed models. Public controversy alone cannot tell us which system works best. Our goal should therefore be a more useful national conversation. Can eligible citizens register and vote? Are procedures applied consistently? Are election officials properly prepared? Can results be checked? Are errors corrected openly? Can disputes be resolved through credible institutions? These questions direct scrutiny towards matters that can strengthen an election. The volume of debate is less important than its quality. A loud accusation may reveal little. A carefully documented discrepancy may reveal a great deal. Ghana needs citizens who ask demanding questions and institutions that can answer them. The people must remain at the centre The experiences of 2016 and 2024 should remain before us whenever debate suggests that a presidential appointment settles the people’s verdict. They remind us that political power is conditional. A government may appoint the chairperson of the Electoral Commission and still fail to secure the electorate’s confidence. That is a reason to respect both the voter and the institutional arrangements through which the voter’s choice is expressed. We should scrutinise appointments. We should insist on impartial commissioners. We should strengthen registration, polling, collation and dispute resolution. We should challenge wrongdoing with evidence and seek reform where experience demonstrates a weakness. Through all of this, we must preserve the central truth of representative government: citizens entrust public office, and citizens retain the authority to withdraw that trust. At the end of an election, a commissioner stands before the nation to announce the result. Long before that announcement, millions of Ghanaians have made the choices from which it must be drawn. The appointment puts the commissioner in office. The ballot puts the government in office.

items.title: Pêche : la Russie vise 100 000 tonnes dans les eaux marocaines
items.description: Moscou espère porter à 100 000 tonnes par an les captures de sa flotte dans les eaux marocaines, contre un quota de 54 000 tonnes cette année. Toute hausse dépendra de la commission mixte russo-marocaine, qui s’appuiera sur les résultats de la campagne scientifique de 45 jours menée par le navire Atlantida. La Russie voit plus grand dans les eaux marocaines. Son Agence fédérale de la pêche (Rosrybolovstvo), chargée de la gestion des ressources halieutiques du pays, a estimé mercredi 28 octobre que les captures de sa flotte pourraient atteindre 100 000 tonnes par an, à condition que la situation de pêche s’améliore. Le quota alloué pour l’année en cours s’élève à 54 000 tonnes. Ce chiffre a été avancé à l’occasion du troisième sommet Russie-Afrique, qui se tient à Moscou les 28 et 29 octobre. La sécurité alimentaire figure parmi les thèmes clés de la rencontre, et la pêche est présentée par l’agence russe comme un domaine où le partenariat avec le continent produit déjà des résultats concrets. Il s’agit toutefois d’une simple perspective : toute augmentation des droits de pêche relève de la commission mixte russo-marocaine, chargée du suivi de l’accord bilatéral. Les 54 000 tonnes correspondent aux droits attribués pour la première année d’application du nouvel accord de pêche conclu entre Rabat et Moscou le 17 octobre 2025. Côté russe, ce volume a été réparti par l’arrêté nº 133 du 23 mars 2026, pris en application du texte. Un mois plus tôt, en février 2026, les deux pays avaient tenu la première réunion de leur commission mixte, instance compétente pour fixer les volumes de capture des années suivantes. Dans la zone marocaine, les armements russes exploitent quatre espèces de petits pélagiques : le maquereau, le chinchard, la sardine et l’anchois. Le Maroc compte parmi les deux pays sur lesquels l’agence dit concentrer une attention particulière, avec la Mauritanie. Dans les eaux mauritaniennes, le régime est différent : les volumes de capture n’y sont pas soumis à quota et les pêcheurs russes y travaillent dans le cadre de contrats commerciaux, principalement pour la sardinelle, le maquereau et le chinchard. Une campagne scientifique de 45 jours Dans le même temps, la Russie a engagé une nouvelle campagne scientifique dans la zone de pêche atlantique du Maroc. Le navire de recherche Atlantida a entamé ses travaux le 26 octobre, après avoir obtenu à Casablanca l’autorisation nécessaire à sa mission. Prévue pour 45 jours, l’expédition comprend 145 opérations de chalutage et des prélèvements sur environ 80 points fixés avec la partie marocaine. Les scientifiques évalueront l’état des stocks de sardine, de maquereau, de chinchard et d’anchois, les quatre espèces au cœur de l’activité de la flotte russe. Les données recueillies doivent permettre de déterminer des volumes de capture scientifiquement fondés. Quarante Russes, dont douze scientifiques, ont embarqué pour la mission aux côtés de deux chercheurs marocains. Les résultats alimenteront les travaux de la commission mixte russo-marocaine, appelée à examiner les futurs volumes de capture autorisés à la flotte russe dans les eaux du Royaume. Cette mission fait suite à la Grande expédition africaine de Rosrybolovstvo, achevée récemment. Menée par deux navires de recherche de la branche atlantique du VNIRO, l’institut russe de recherche halieutique et océanographique, dont l’Atlantida, elle a mobilisé à bord, aux côtés des équipes russes, des scientifiques de plusieurs pays africains. L’agence russe lui attribue une portée à la fois scientifique et politique, puisqu’elle contribue selon elle à consolider la position de la Russie dans l’océan mondial, et affirme en avoir tiré un matériel inédit sur l’état des stocks. The post Pêche : la Russie vise 100 000 tonnes dans les eaux marocaines appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Neville warns managers can need sacking ‘for their own good’ as Carrick fights on
items.description: Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to dismissed “for their own good” as Manchester United persist with under-pressure boss Michael Carrick. Carrick’s future at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation after a miserable run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 humbling at home to Bournemouth left the English giants one point above the Premier League relegation zone. United have won just two of 12 matches in all competitions this season, with a return of seven points from eight league games representing their worst start to a league season in 40 years. But former United and England midfielder Carrick, 45, remains in charge and is expected to give a pre-match press conference later Thursday ahead of the team’s league match away to Chelsea on Saturday. “I reckon what’s happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is that they (the United hierarchy) literally debated it (Carrick’s future) back and forth,” former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick to Football podcast. “I don’t know this, but they’ve debated it to the point where they’ve got themselves into a muddle, and thought, ‘we’ll just stay with him’. “I think staying with him is a result of the lack of planning, the lack of probably available options, the lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available. That’s when you’re really struggling.” Neville, a former United team-mate of Carrick, added: “Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia. I was happy that they put me out of my misery.” – ‘Enough is enough’ – Both Eddie Howe, previously in charge of Newcastle, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann have been touted as possible replacements for Carrick at Old Trafford. Carrick, however, appears to have the backing of the United faithful, being warmly applauded by fans as he made his way down the tunnel following the defeat by Bournemouth. Moments later a chorus of boos erupted as the players left the pitch as supporters made clear where they think the blame lies for United’s current malaise. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after inspiring an impressive revival following the team’s struggles under Ruben Amorim — United secured third place in the Premier League and a return to the Champions League. The drastic decline this season is an all-too-familiar story for United supporters, who last witnessed a Premier League title triumph 13 years ago under Alex Ferguson. Neville believes the root of United’s woes is majority owners the Glazer family, saying “enough is enough” as he urged them to sell-up. The Glazers took control of the club in a controversial takeover in 2005. They remain majority owners after selling a minority stake to British billionaire businessman Jim Ratcliffe in 2024 . Neville, a longstanding critic, reiterated his call for the US-based family to sell. “There’s £1.2 billion ($1.6 billion) of debt in that football club, they’re hamstrung in some ways,” said Neville, adding: “You’ve got a failure of 13, 14 years on the football side, you’ve subbed it out to somebody else (Ratcliffe), which is ridiculous, and not took responsibility…Enough is enough, they have to sell the whole the club. The fans have had enough. They have to go now.” The post Neville warns managers can need sacking ‘for their own good’ as Carrick fights on appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Los fetiches de Meirás arrasan: desde el maletín del dictador hasta el joyero de Carmencita
items.description: Estaba claro que el maletín del dictador iba a arrasar en la subasta, pero nadie se imaginó que su puja fuera a estar tan reñida. Acababan de ser subastadas, también a precios desorbitados, otras de las piezas estrella de la tarde, como la raqueta o los palos de golf del pazo de Meirás. Y entonces llegó el maletín a la sala, y con él la tensión, las risas nerviosas del personal y el pasmo. No se ha dado, ni siquiera, garantía de que Francisco Franco Bahamonde llegase alguna vez en su vida a usar ese objeto. Un maletín de cuero marrón perfectamente conservado que lleva en la solapa una dedicatoria grabada en letras doradas: “Al Generalísimo Franco Caudillo de España y Jefe Nacional de Falange Española Tradicionalista y de las J.O.N.S ”. La cartera partía en el catálogo de la casa madrileña Magna Art Auctions a un precio de salida de 350 euros. Y en un par de minutos —después de dar unos segundos a los aspirantes para “pensar” hasta dónde podían llegar— el “maletín personal” se acabó adjudicando por 19.000 a un pujador invisible, que ofreció ese dinero por la web. La sala rompió en aplausos para celebrar la buena venta después de que la encargada de pastorear la puja diese la enhorabuena al agraciado. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Private sector benefiting from low lending rates – BoG Governor
items.description: Average lending rates in Ghana have declined from 30.25% in December 2024 to 15.7% in September 2026, while private sector credit growth has strengthened to 26.4%, according to the Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama. Speaking at the launch of the Ghana in Numbers 2025 publication in Accra, he said the improvements reflected gains in macroeconomic stability and financing conditions for businesses. “These gains are also reflected in improved credit conditions,” Dr Asiama said, noting that growth in real private sector credit had risen from less than 1% about two years ago to 26.4% at the end of September 2026. He said inflation had remained in single digits for 13 consecutive months, while the exchange rate was relatively stable. “Inflation is low and has been in single digits for 13 consecutive months so far. The exchange rate is relatively stable, notwithstanding the external headwinds that we face. And of course, banking sector resilience has improved significantly over the past two years,” he said. The decline in lending rates could ease borrowing costs for businesses seeking funds for expansion and investment, although access to affordable credit remains important, particularly for smaller enterprises. Dr Asiama said the central bank was pursuing initiatives to expand financial inclusion and make formal financial services more accessible to underserved groups. “These efforts are intended to make formal financial services more accessible, more affordable and convenient, particularly for young people, for women, for the micro, small and medium-sized enterprises and underserved communities,” he said. He added that Ghana’s large youth population presented opportunities for entrepreneurship but required the right support to translate into economic gains. “Our large youth population presents a significant source of innovation and entrepreneurship. However, realising this demographic potential will depend on our ability to equip them with relevant skills, support enterprise development and create an enabling environment for investment,” he said. The Governor also disclosed that the Bank of Ghana was developing a directive to regulate artificial intelligence in the financial sector. “We want to promote innovation but at the same time address the emerging risks that can evolve from this,” he said. Dr Asiama said reliable statistics remained essential for monetary policy, financial regulation and investment decisions, commending the Ghana Statistical Service for bringing key economic and financial indicators together in the Ghana in Numbers 2025 publication.

items.title: Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment
items.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has praised President Bola Tinubu following a Federal High Court judgment recognising him as the All Progressives Congress candidate for Imo West Senatorial District, saying the ruling has broken the shackles holding the state. Okorocha spoke on Thursday while hosting his legal team after the judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court in Abuja. The court ruled that Okorocha won the APC senatorial primary conducted on May 18, 2026, and ordered the party to submit his name to the Independent National Electoral Commission as its candidate for the January 16, 2027 senatorial election. The court also directed Governor Hope Uzodimma to stop parading himself as the party’s candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Okorocha thanked the judiciary for standing on the side of justice, describing the outcome as a victory for the people of Imo State. “I thank the judiciary for standing on the side of justice. I could imagine what would have happened in the state if they decided to twist justice. This is a victory for Imo State,” he said. The former governor also linked the judgment to the symbolic shackle on Tinubu’s traditional cap, suggesting that the President’s position had become clearer through the court’s decision. “This is also the first time the Imo people will understand the sign of the shackle on President Tinubu’s cap. By this judgment, the shackle on Imo State has been broken, and it is also evident that the President is tired of this nonsense and that he is not in support of it,” Okorocha said. He expressed gratitude to Tinubu, although he did not provide direct evidence that the President had intervened in the legal dispute or influenced the court’s decision. The judgment followed a legal battle in which Okorocha challenged INEC’s recognition of Uzodimma as the APC’s candidate for Imo West. The dispute attracted further attention earlier this month after INEC petitioned the police and the Department of State Services over a disputed document circulating online that purported to name Okorocha as the winner of the primary. INEC maintained that its official report recognised Uzodimma as the winner. Okorocha also addressed reports surrounding his alleged arrest, saying he deliberately refrained from commenting when the news broke. “When the news broke out that I was arrested, I refused to make any comments,” he said. He, however, questioned the documents presented during the dispute over the APC primary, particularly the claims that Uzodimma emerged through consensus and the discrepancies he alleged in the dates recorded in the documents. Okorocha questioned how a document could indicate that Uzodimma emerged through consensus when, according to him, individual scores were recorded. He also raised questions about a document he said listed the primary election date as May 16, rather than May 18, when the exercise was held. “So which one did the court really dwell on?” he asked, seeking clarification on the documentary evidence underpinning the dispute. The controversy had intensified after INEC maintained that the official result submitted to its headquarters showed Uzodimma winning with 230,464 votes against Okorocha’s 1,098 votes. The commission subsequently asked security agencies to investigate the circulation of a different document purportedly naming Okorocha as the winner. The latest judgment marks a significant development in the contest for the APC ticket in Imo West ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ghana records nearly 14,000 new HIV infections in 2025 as condom use declines
items.description: Ghana recorded 13,951 new HIV infections in 2025, with women accounting for nearly two-thirds of the cases, as health authorities warn that risky sexual behaviour and declining condom use are driving new infections. Greater Accra recorded the highest number of new infections, with 3,141 cases, according to figures presented by the Ghana AIDS Commission. The figures have raised concerns about the country’s progress in controlling the spread of HIV, with the Commission warning that Ghana remains off track to achieve the global 95-95-95 targets under its 2026–2030 National Strategic Plan. Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation at the Ghana AIDS Commission, Isaiah Doe Kwao, said there was an urgent need to strengthen prevention, testing and treatment efforts to reverse the trend. Speaking at the 2026 HIV and AIDS Partnership Forum, he highlighted the factors contributing to new infections and called for greater public awareness and financial support for the national HIV response. Of the 13,951 new infections recorded in 2025, women accounted for 8,900, representing 63.8 per cent of the total. Greater Accra had the highest number of new infections, with 3,141 cases. The region also had the largest population of people living with HIV, reflecting its high population concentration. Mr Kwao said national statistics showed that slightly more than 330,000 people were living with HIV across Ghana at the end of 2025, with Greater Accra accounting for more than 77,000 cases. He said the concentration of people in major population centres, alongside patterns of sexual behaviour, partly explained the high numbers recorded in these areas. “This is important because in populations where there are more people, you realise that more people are engaging in heterosexual sex, which is the highest mode of transmission,” he said. He added, however, that the key concern should be how to reduce new infections rather than simply focus on the numbers. “But the most important is what are we doing to reduce these numbers?” he asked. Mr Kwao identified risky sexual behaviour, including sex without condoms and having multiple sexual partners, as major factors contributing to the spread of HIV. He cited casual sexual encounters and relationships outside committed partnerships as examples of behaviours that could increase the risk of infection. “For example, side chickism, hookups, people having sex without using a condom. This is one of the most critical transmission modes to get HIV and AIDS,” he said. He urged sexually active people to know their HIV status, use condoms consistently and avoid behaviours that could expose them to infection. “If you should go and test, if you test and you are negative, you live a non-risky life. You stick to your partner. It’s as simple as that. And be faithful to your partner,” he said. Mr Kwao also acknowledged that HIV could be transmitted through other routes, including from mother to child during pregnancy, childbirth or breastfeeding. However, he said that preventing sexual transmission remained a key part of efforts to reduce new infections. The Ghana AIDS Commission has warned that the country is not on course to meet the global 95-95-95 HIV targets under its 2026–2030 National Strategic Plan. The targets seek to ensure that 95 per cent of people living with HIV know their status, 95 per cent of those diagnosed receive sustained antiretroviral treatment, and 95 per cent of people receiving treatment achieve viral suppression. Achieving these targets is considered critical to reducing HIV-related illness and deaths and preventing further transmission. Mr Kwao said intensified prevention, testing and treatment programmes would be necessary to improve Ghana’s performance. The latest figures highlight the need to reach more people with HIV testing services, encourage early diagnosis and ensure that those who test positive can access and remain on treatment. Public education will also be important in addressing misconceptions about HIV and encouraging safer sexual practices. Beyond prevention and treatment, Mr Kwao said inadequate funding posed a challenge to Ghana’s efforts to meet its HIV targets. He noted that donor fatigue was becoming a concern and called on the government to increase its financial contribution to the national HIV and AIDS response. “But now donor fatigue is setting in. That is why we are encouraging government to increase its financing for the national HIV and AIDS response,” he said. Mr Kwao said the Commission was advocating an increase in the share of the District Assemblies Common Fund allocated to HIV and AIDS programmes to strengthen prevention and support services at the local level. He explained that greater funding for district-level interventions would help ensure that resources reached communities where they were needed most. The Commission is also seeking to strengthen the National HIV and AIDS Fund, which he said needed additional contributions to support its work. “We are hoping with government support we can be able to engage the private sector so that they can contribute more to the fund through their social corporate responsibility,” he said. He added that the Resource Mobilisation Committee of the Ghana AIDS Board was being encouraged to use its expertise to attract more funding and help bridge the financial gap. According to Mr Kwao, additional resources would be necessary to support the programmes required to meet both national and international HIV targets. Mr Kwao also appealed to individuals to contribute to the National HIV and AIDS Fund, stressing that collective support was needed to sustain prevention and treatment programmes. He said even small donations could help strengthen the country’s response to the epidemic. “Your 1 cedi can go a long way to help the fund because HIV can affect not only you, but also your family,” he said. He encouraged members of the public to use the short code *9898# to make contributions to the fund. “You can also contribute if it’s 1 cedi, 10 cedis, 1 million. We accept so that we can raise funds to bridge the gap that we need to finance the HIV,” he added.

items.title: Un business éclatant
items.description: Les laveries, blanchisseries ou pressings se multiplient dans les quartiers dakarois, séduisant une clientèle en quête de gain de temps. Derrière ce commerce florissant, les investisseurs font face à de nombreux défis : loyers en hausse, factures d'électricité élevées, produits détergents coûteux et machines souvent en panne. Dans les ruelles animées de la Médina, quartier populaire de Dakar, l’animation ne faiblit jamais. Les vendeurs de café interpellent les passants, tandis que motos et véhicules se disputent des routes étroites, créant de longs embouteillages. C’est dans cette atmosphère bruyante que s’est implanté un phénomène grandissant : les laveries, également appelées pressing ou blanchisseries. Discrètes ou ostensibles, elles ont investi presque tous les coins des quartiers de la capitale, proposant des services allant du simple lavage au repassage complet. Automatiques ou traditionnels, ces établissements attirent une clientèle de plus en plus nombreuse, séduite par la commodité d’un service clé en main. Devant son magasin situé au cœur de la Médina, Alpha Bâ supervise son équipe de trois employés. Des vêtements déjà lavés sèchent au soleil, exposés à la vue de tous. À l’intérieur, l’espace est encombré de sacs en plastique contenant des vêtements de toutes sortes et de qualités diverses. Le bruit des machines à laver perturbe parfois les conversations. Voilà plus de cinq ans que cet homme au teint clair dirige son affaire, qu’il dit « rentable malgré les difficultés ». « J’ai hérité de deux grandes machines, mais j’en ai acheté deux autres d’occasion : l'une à 200.000 FCfa et l’autre à 125.000 FCfa », confie-t-il. Des tarifs diversifiés Son activité consiste à accueillir les clients venus déposer leur linge sale, qu’il pèse avant de convenir d’un prix. En effet, chez Alpha Bâ, la tarification est négociable. Face à la rareté des clients, certains jours, il accepte des prix revus à la baisse pour garantir un chiffre d’affaires minimal. Les services proposés se déclinent en trois formules : le lavage seul, le lavage avec séchage et le service complet incluant le repassage. « Pour le lavage sans séchage, c’est entre 200 et 300 FCfa le kilogramme. Avec séchage, comptez entre 400 et 600 FCfa. Et pour le lavage, séchage et repassage, le tarif est de 750 à 800 FCfa le kilogramme », détaille-t-il. Le mode de paiement varie selon les clients. Certains règlent la totalité après pesée, d’autres versent la moitié et s’acquittent du reste au retrait, tandis que quelques-uns ne paient qu’à la récupération du linge. À quelques pas de là, Moulay Salif Diallo gère sa propre laverie avec l’aide de sa sœur. Malgré les klaxons incessants et les eaux usées stagnantes devant son local, il vaque à ses occupations. En sueur, il explique utiliser quatre machines : deux pour le lavage, une combinant lavage et séchage et une autre faisant du séchage uniquement. Un fer à repasser complète l’équipement. « La machine à sécher m’a coûté 80.000 FCfa ; celle qui fait le lavage et le séchage, entre 150.000 et 200.000 FCfa, et celles pour le lavage seul, 90.000 FCfa chacune », précise-t-il. Toutes ont été acquises d’occasion, à l’exception de la balance, achetée neuve à 14.000 FCfa. Contrairement à Alpha Bâ, Moulay Salif Diallo applique des prix fixes : 300 FCfa pour le lavage simple, 500 FCfa pour le lavage avec séchage et 800 FCfa pour le service complet incluant le repassage. « Les nouveaux clients paient intégralement après pesée. Pour les habitués, je fais parfois preuve de compréhension », affirme-t-il. À Fass, non loin de la Médina, une atmosphère similaire règne. Chez l’un des points de laverie automatique de l’entreprise « Fotall service », les machines industrielles sont installées à ciel ouvert. Lissa Sarr, la directrice commerciale, indique que ces machines sont de deux catégories : celles pouvant contenir un volume de 9 kg et d’autres de 20 kg. « Pour un volume de 9 kg, le lavage et le séchage sont facturés à 4.500 FCfa. Si on y ajoute le repassage, le client doit débourser 3.000 FCfa de plus ; ce qui fait un total de 7.500 FCfa. Pour les 20 kg, le lavage et le séchage sont à 6.000 FCfa, et le repassage à 5.000 FCfa », détaille-t-elle. L’entreprise compte environ une trentaine d’employés, ajoute Lissa Sarr. Pape Ndiaye, client fidèle depuis plus de deux ans, ne tarit pas d’éloges sur ces services. Auparavant, il devait faire appel à une lingère à domicile. « Mais, tu sais ce que ça coûte ? Il fallait payer le lavage, acheter le repas pour la personne, sans oublier les détergents et les petites dépenses qui s’accumulent. Le pire, c’était le temps que je perdais », se souvient-il. Désormais, il dépose son linge le matin et le récupère propre, plié et prêt à porter. « Je gagne au moins une demi-journée par semaine », affirme-t-il. Pape reste toutefois lucide : toutes les laveries ne se valent pas. « Tu récupères parfois ton linge et tu te demandes si ça a vraiment été lavé », lâche-t-il. Selon lui, le choix de l’adresse est primordial. Derrière ces tarifications et ces chiffres d’affaires se cachent des difficultés pesantes pour les investisseurs. Alpha Bâ évoque en premier lieu le coût du loyer. « Depuis que j’occupe les lieux, le loyer est passé de 125.000 à 250.000 FCfa par mois. J’en ai parlé plusieurs fois avec mon bailleur, mais il refuse de revoir le montant à la baisse », déplore-t-il. Des difficultés ne manquent pas Le coût de l’électricité représente une charge supplémentaire considérable. « Malgré un budget quotidien de 5000 FCfa, il arrive que la recharge ne couvre pas l'ensemble de la journée », fustige Alpha. S’y ajoutent les dépenses en produits détergents : lessive en poudre, désinfectant, savon liquide dont le bidon de 20 litres peut atteindre 30.000 FCfa. Un autre problème, plus inattendu, est soulevé par Alpha Bâ : certains clients déposent leur linge et ne reviennent jamais. « Les vêtements peuvent rester ici indéfiniment sans que leur propriétaire ne vienne les récupérer », fait-il savoir. Pour Moulay Salif, les difficultés sont similaires : loyer, eau, électricité et machines qui tombent souvent en panne. Pour son local exigu, il paie 200.000 FCfa de loyer mensuel et recharge au minimum 5.000 FCfa d’électricité par jour. Malgré ces obstacles, ces entrepreneurs continuent de faire tourner leurs affaires, convaincus que ce secteur en pleine expansion offre encore de belles perspectives. Par Aziz Méthiour NDIAYE (Stagiaire)

items.title: ‘A Man Must Eat Meat’
items.description: In the Texas race for U.S. Senate, Republicans keep coming back to the same insult: that James Talarico, the Democratic candidate, does not eat meat. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has referred to his opponent as “ Tofu Talarico .” Donald Trump has repeatedly called Talarico a vegan—sometimes pronouncing it “ vay-gan ,” and sometimes embellishing it with the assertion that Talarico does eat meat, but that afterward , he “throws up all over the place.” At one October rally, the president said of Talarico, “In Texas he talks about, I’m a vegan, I’m a vegan ,” and then helpfully explained, “ vegan meaning he likes lettuce.” For the record, Talarico is not a vegan. He has denied being one repeatedly, and as a visual rebuttal, his campaign posted a picture of him chomping on a turkey leg. His critics may be basing their attacks on some statements Talarico made during his 2022 campaign for reelection to the Texas House of Representatives. In one speech, he said that reducing meat consumption is the “moral thing to do,” and that his campaign had become a “nonmeat campaign” that was buying only “vegan products from our local vegan businesses.” But he has said his current campaign “basically runs on barbecue,” and unless he means tempeh burgers, this means it is not vegan. Nevertheless, Senator Ted Cruz played a clip of the 2022 speech on a recent podcast episode and cited it as evidence that Talarico wants to “destroy oil and gas and destroy cattle ranching.” The conservative commentator Sean Hannity said on his podcast last month that Talarico is running a “vegan campaign.” [ Read: All the president’s hotties ] The plant-based criticisms seem to be less about Talarico’s diet and more an attempt to undermine his masculinity. Manliness is still a trait that many American voters look for in their male leaders, and a beefy corpus of psychological literature reveals that people subconsciously associate meat-eating with masculinity. And although this bias exists almost everywhere, it’s particularly prevalent in Texas, the nation’s biggest cattle-producing state, where brisket is such a way of life that Texas Monthly magazine has a “ barbecue editor . ” Studies conducted across more than a dozen countries, and with excellent titles such as “Eating Meat Makes You Sexy,” have found that people consider meat eaters to be more masculine than vegetarians, and especially more so than vegans. These studies have concluded that eating meat makes men “feel like real men” ; that women prefer omnivorous men and rate them as more attractive; and that men who want to be seen as more masculine are less likely to consider giving up meat. “There is a metaphoric relationship between mammal muscle meat and maleness” is how one such study vividly put it. In the United States, women are more likely to be vegetarian or vegan than men are. Even female vegans think male vegans are more feminine than meat-eating men, which shows how “deeply rooted in our consciousness” these stereotypes are, Dominika Adamczyk, a psychologist at the Institute of Psychology of the Polish Academy of Sciences who has conducted several studies on meat-eating and perceptions of masculinity in Poland, told me. Veganism might seem female-coded because it connotes empathy and a concern about animal welfare, which may be positive qualities in general but are not exactly Texas tough. Vegan men seem to violate the stereotype that men should be strong, ruthless killers. The accusations that Talarico is a vegan invoke “this idea that compassion, particularly with animals, is kind of incompatible with masculinity,” Rob Velzeboer, a Ph.D. candidate at the University of British Columbia who has co-authored a review of the meat-masculinity studies, told me. Veganism seems more socially acceptable when men pursue it for health reasons rather than animal-welfare reasons, Velzeboer added. Politicians seem to be well aware of what their diet implies about their manliness. Men running for office from both parties have long made sure to ostentatiously eat meat on camera. George H. W. Bush liked to order a rare T-bone steak while campaigning. In 2003, John Kerry chowed on a cheesesteak in Philly (though, controversially, with Swiss cheese rather than Cheez Whiz) a few weeks before he announced he was running for president. And practically all Oval Office hopefuls stop by the Iowa State Fair to gnaw on a pork chop . Meanwhile, the mere suggestion of salad can lead to an entire news cycle: After Barack Obama remarked on the high price of arugula in 2007, during his campaign for president, a spokesperson for his Republican rival John McCain derided him as an “arugula-eating, pointy-headed-professor type.” [ Read: Radical vegans are trying to change your diet ] Like Obama before him, Talarico may overcome this attack. But the stereotype that a good, strong leader eats meat will likely stick around. On some lizard-brain level, many people appreciate a man who seems like he can slay a bison and drag its carcass back to the cave for dinner. Reading the psychological literature, I was shocked by just how many people around the world have an innate association between animal protein and machismo. But perhaps I shouldn’t have been: Many years ago, I visited Russia, my birthplace and another culture that insists on manly meat-eating. One day my husband, Rich, and I sat down with my Russian cousin at a mostly vegetarian St. Petersburg restaurant for lunch. Scanning the menu, my cousin grew more and more uneasy. “I don’t know if this place will have the right food for Richard,” she said. “A man must eat meat.”

Fact check: Viral video of JUI-F chief asking for forgiveness in NA is doctored
items.description: Several social media users, including PML-N supporters based on their past posts, shared a video on X on October 28 allegedly showing Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman asking for forgiveness in the National Assembly amid his tensions with the government. However, the video is doctored using AI. Fazl on Oct 28 accused the federal government of misusing the Constitution by imposing governor’s rule and an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Speaking in the National Assembly, he argued that the measures amounted to a forced transfer of power rather than change through public opinion. He also criticised Defence Minister Khawaja Asif for failing to protect the sanctity of Parliament and called for a new Charter of Democracy to prevent unconstitutional actions and political violence. He also recounted his efforts to ease tensions between the federal government and the PTI, claiming that the government had abandoned attempts to reach a consensus. He rejected questions about his patriotism, highlighting his party’s sacrifices in the fight against terrorism and condemning the ridicule of martyrs. The JUI-F chief has recently been consistently criticised by government officials for his criticism of the state and support of the PTI. On Oct 28, a pro-PML-N account, based on its past posts, shared a video on X, allegedly showing Fazl asking for forgiveness in the National Assembly, with the following caption: “See how Fazlu kept grovelling in the assembly today for forgiveness, but no one will share this part of the speech.” The post garnered 20,277 views. In the clip, Fazl can be heard saying: “What is my fault? Why are they after me? I have asked for forgiveness, but they are not accepting it. Is my sin greater than PTI? What did I do wrong? Why am I being treated unjustly? These are the questions you should ask the media. But you are not doing it.” Another PML-N supporter, based on their bio and past posts, shared the same video with the following caption: “All the antics, today in the assembly, the ripples of apology. Fazlu’s politics is also masterful — where he needs to show off, his speeches go viral, and where he has to apologise, the camera, workers, and share button all vanish. Just spread this clip too; the public has the right to see the full film.” The post garnered 12,785 views. Jalal Sherazi, who identifies himself as a coordinator in the Prime Minister’s Office in his bio, shared the same video with the caption, “Look, even today, Fazlur Rehman kept talking about demanding an apology in the assembly, but this part of his speech is being avoided from being shared on social media.” The post garnered 1,775 views. Shahzad Younas Sheikh, who, according to his X bio, is a former spokesperson for Punjab, also shared the video with the caption: “See how Fazlu kept mumbling apologies in the assembly even today, but no one shares this bit of his speech.” The post garnered 661 views. Similarly, several other PML-N supporters, based on their past posts, shared the same video in a similar context on X, as can be seen here , here , and here . A fact check was initiated to determine the veracity of the claim due to keen public interest in the tense relations between the JUI-F chief and the government amid his support for the PTI and criticism of the Centre’s actions in KP. A keyword search conducted to determine whether credible mainstream media outlets had reported the alleged remarks yielded no results to corroborate them. Investigating the clip showed discrepancies in the synchronisation between the audio and Fazl’s lip movements, suggesting that the video appeared to be dubbed. The viral video was then analysed using AI detection tools. Diopter, an AI audio detection tool, flagged the audio as 100 per cent AI-generated. Another audio detection tool, Deepfake Total, detected a 75.6pc likelihood of AI manipulation. Hive also showed a 92pc likelihood of AI-generated speech. Similarly, the SORA AI Video Detector flagged the video as 66.67pc AI-generated. Meanwhile, Meta AI’s detector identified a digital watermark in the clip, suggesting that it had been generated using OpenAI. A reverse image search conducted to trace the original clip yielded a video posted on the National Assembly of Pakistan ’s official YouTube account, dated October 28, 2026, with the following title: ‘JUI F chief/MNA Maulana Fazal Ur Rehman expresses his views during National Assembly Session.’ The viral clip starts at the 3:25-minute mark and continues until 3:51. In the original clip, Fazal said, “Gauhar Sahib was also there; Asad Qaisar Sahib was also there. And he said to me that if they are calling you and you wish to meet them and if there is any further discussion on this topic, then we are 100pc ready to accept your mandate. “Although I have not met the prime minister for the past four to five months. And for the purpose that I can save the citizens of Pakistan from their blood, save the country from extremism, pave the way for the government and pave the way for the opposition, and that the country does not go towards bloodshed.” At no point in his entire speech did he apologise or make such remarks as shown in the viral video. The same was also corroborated by a keyword search that yielded a news report from the Express Tribune , dated October 29, 2026, with the following title, ‘Fazl calls for new Charter of Democracy.’ As per the report, the JUI-F chief urged political forces to resolve their differences through dialogue rather than resorting to unconstitutional measures or violence. Further searches also yielded the original video shared by Jamiat Digital Media on X on October 28, 2026. The clip, too, contained no apology or any such remarks. The claim that a viral video shows JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman asking for forgiveness in the National Assembly is false. The clip is doctored and has been dubbed over using AI.

items.title: CRIEF : le procès de Mandian Sidibé et Cie s’ouvre ce vendredi
items.description: Sauf changement de dernière minute, les débats dans l’affaire opposant le parquet spécial à l’ancien directeur général de l’Office guinéen de publicité (OGP), Mandian Sidibé, et à ses co-prévenus s’ouvriront ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026 devant la chambre de jugement de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF). L’ancien patron de l’OGP est poursuivi aux côtés de Pépé Haba et du comptable Aboubacar Sidiki Konaté pour des faits présumés de détournement de deniers publics, d’abus de fonction, de corruption, d’atteinte à la liberté d’accès et à l’égalité des candidats dans les marchés publics, d’usage illicite de biens par l’octroi d’avantages injustifiés, de concussion et de complicité. Le montant en cause est estimé à 78 milliards de francs guinéens. Pour rappel, le 15 juin dernier, la chambre de jugement de la CRIEF avait ordonné la remise en liberté de Mandian Sidibé pour des raisons de santé, après plus d’un an de détention, tout en le plaçant sous contrôle judiciaire. Elisa Camara L’article CRIEF : le procès de Mandian Sidibé et Cie s’ouvre ce vendredi est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Jamais dire jamais : Peskov sur les choix européens concernant le gaz russe
items.description: « Ils sont en train de scier la branche sur laquelle ils etaient assis. » C'est ainsi que le porte-parole du Kremlin Dmitri Peskov a commente la position de Bruxelles concernant le gaz russe. Il a critique le refus de l'Union europeenne (UE) de reprendre ses importations, meme si la situation en Ukraine venait a evoluer. Interroge le 29 octobre par le media russe Izvestia sur l'abandon des approvisionnements russes et le maintien a l'arret des gazoducs Nord Stream, il a juge une telle ligne politique contraire aux interets economiques des Europeens. Selon lui, l'economie europeenne stagne. Elle conserve une puissance considerable, mais l'energie russe bon marche, en particulier le gaz livre par gazoduc, a longtemps soutenu sa competitivite et sa prosperite. En s'en privant, les pays de l'UE renoncent a un avantage dont beneficiaient leurs usines comme leurs consommateurs. L'UE maintient pourtant son calendrier de sortie. Le reglement adopte en janvier 2026 prevoit la fin des importations de gaz naturel liquefie russe sous contrats a long terme debut 2027, puis celles du gaz achemine par gazoduc a l'automne. En 2025, la Russie representait encore environ 13 % du gaz importe par les Vingt-Sept. Moscou se dit ouvert a la discussion. Le 26 octobre, le porte-parole du Kremlin avait explique que la Russie pourrait examiner de nouvelles livraisons en cas d'interet europeen et de volumes disponibles, une partie du gaz etant desormais orientee vers d'autres marches. Face a la volonte de Bruxelles d'exclure tout retour en arriere , il a insiste sur le caractere imprudent d'un engagement definitif : « Dire qu'ils n'acheteront jamais [de ressources energetiques russes] ? Le mot "jamais" n'a pas sa place dans les relations entre etats. Il ne devrait pas. » La question du coût de l'energie revient au premier plan. Le 28 octobre, le prix de reference du gaz sur la plateforme neerlandaise Title Transfer Facility a brievement atteint 100 euros le megawattheure, pour la premiere fois depuis decembre 2022. Les perturbations du transport de gaz naturel liquefie depuis le Moyen-Orient ont contribue a la hausse. Pour l'industrie europeenne, notamment la chimie et la siderurgie, le rencherissement du combustible constitue une pression supplementaire.

'Absolutely absurd verdict': Lawyers, journalists react to Imaan, Hadi's sentencing in security breach case
items.description: Human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, were convicted for the second time in less than a year on Thursday. This time, the couple was sentenced to 10 years in a security breach case following a jail trial. The 2024 case pertained to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7. After an anti-terrorism court pronounced them guilty, journalists and lawyers raised questions and expressed reservations. Legal adviser for the International Commission of Jurists Reema Omer termed the convictions “cruel, vindictive and textbook examples of using law and the judicial process as weapons of persecution”. “Imaan and Hadi are prisoners of conscience,” she posted on X. Lawyer Rida Hosain said the convictions were “a stain on our judicial system”. “Those entrusted with upholding the rule of law are weaponising it to persecute courageous human rights lawyers. “This only further exposes a system that is functioning as an instrument of repression,” she said. Op-ed editor at The News , Zebunnisa Burki, reacted to the development with “beyond ridiculous”. Journalist Zarrar Khuhro also pointed out that the couple was sentenced to 10 years for “removing a barrier”. “A decade in jail is what rapists usually get,” he said. Journalist Asma Shirazi reacted to the news by calling it “reprehensible and regrettable”. Journalist Maryam Nawaz Khan criticised the judgement saying: “A sham/ secret trial delivers a sham sentence. Imaan Mazari and Hadi Ali Chattha, two human rights lawyers, sentenced to 10 years in prison over road barriers they maintain they never removed. First, their tweets; now, this. Criminalising dissent and persecuting lawyers is an assault on fundamental rights and constitutional freedoms. This sentence is outrageous and unlawful.” Academic Nida Kirmani said the couple was “paying the price for standing up to a cruel and vindictive state run by petty men with fragile egos”. “Absolutely absurd verdict,” she said. Journalist Saqib Bashir said the couple was sentenced without a “transparent” trial. “This is a mockery of the judiciary and the justice system; it is a judicial murder of dissenting voices,” former Jamaat-i-Islami senator Mushtaq Ahmed said. “Imaan and Hadi are strong voices against enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings and that is their only crime,” he said. “Those who speak up for justice face jail. Those who justify the state’s dictatorial actions ascend to higher positions,” journalist Veengas said. The National Commission for Human Rights also expressed serious concern, saying the right to a fair trial, due process and effective judicial remedies must be fully protected. “The severity of the sentences raises concerns about proportionality and the protection of fundamental rights,” the commission said.

items.title: Littérature : Le matrimoine au cœur d’un dialogue entre trois auteures du Fil d’Ariane Éditions
items.description: À l’occasion du Salon du livre féminin de Dakar , la maison d’édition Le Fil d’Ariane a réuni trois auteures autour du matrimoine, de la transmission et de la place des femmes dans les relations familiales. À travers leurs œuvres, Rokhy Ndiaye , Mame Anta Mbacké et Angelina Uloma Nwachukwu interrogent les responsabilités conjugales, la liberté de choisir et les réalités parfois insoupçonnées de la vie intime. Le matrimoine ne se limite pas à l’héritage matériel ou à la mémoire des femmes qui ont marqué l’histoire. Il se transmet également à travers les récits, les expériences familiales et les enseignements légués d’une génération à l’autre. C’est autour de cette conception que s’est articulée la rencontre littéraire organisée par Le Fil d’Ariane Éditions, en marge du Salon du livre féminin de Dakar, placé cette année sous le thème du matrimoine. À l’initiative de Mame Ngoné Faye, fondatrice de cette maison d’édition, trois auteures ont croisé leurs regards sur des questions qui traversent la vie des femmes : les responsabilités dans le couple, le choix du conjoint, la place de l’amour dans le mariage et les secrets qui peuvent subsister au sein d’une famille. Une démarche qui a permis de mettre en perspective les univers de leurs ouvrages et les réflexions qu’ils suscitent. « Je me suis dit, comme nous sommes dans le cadre du Salon du livre féminin de Dakar et que cette année, le thème porte sur le matrimoine, j’ai regardé dans mon catalogue et je me suis dit : tiens, il y a trois ouvrages qui se recoupent », débute Mame Ngoné Faye. La rencontre a ainsi donné lieu à un dialogue entre Rokhy Ndiaye , auteure d’Entre soupirs et sourires, Mame Anta Mbacké, qui signe La Soxna, et Angelina Uloma Nwachukwu, dont son ouvrage Fissures d’or a également été présenté au cours des échanges. Au-delà de leurs différences narratives, ces textes accordent une place centrale aux femmes et à leurs expériences, tout en questionnant les rapports humains. La responsabilité conjugale au-delà des obligations matérielles Dans La Soxna, Mame Anta Mbacké met en scène Bassirou, un homme partagé entre ses obligations professionnelles et ses responsabilités familiales. Alors que sa première épouse, Soxna, gravement malade, a besoin de lui, il envisage de se contenter de lui envoyer de l’argent, hésitant à se rendre à son chevet. Cette attitude révèle les limites d’une conception du devoir conjugal qui privilégie les moyens matériels au détriment de la présence et de l’accompagnement. Pour l’auteure, la situation du personnage permet notamment d’interroger la responsabilité de l’époux et le rôle de la mère dans la transmission des valeurs familiales. « Une personne malade n’a pas besoin que de matériel, que d’argent. Sa maman lui a fait comprendre que sa femme avait besoin de sa présence physique », explique Mame Anta Mbacké lors des échanges. Dans le récit, la mère de Bassirou refuse de le laisser se soustraire à ses obligations. Elle l’encourage à rejoindre son épouse et à prendre conscience de ce que son absence peut lui coûter. La figure maternelle apparaît ainsi comme un vecteur de transmission, capable de rappeler à la génération suivante les exigences morales de la vie familiale. Le roman aborde également la difficulté de communiquer au sein du couple. À travers Sorna, qui finit par exprimer la souffrance longtemps gardée en elle, Mame Anta Mbacké met en lumière la nécessité d’une écoute véritable entre époux. La parole féminine, longtemps contenue, devient alors un moyen de faire émerger des vérités indispensables à la compréhension de l’autre. Le droit de choisir leur vie Avec Entre soupirs et sourires, Rokhy Ndiaye s’intéresse aux critères qui orientent le choix d’un conjoint. Son récit met en scène une jeune femme qui hésite à s’engager dans le mariage avec un homme pourtant décrit comme gentil, pieux et attentionné. À travers cette hésitation, l’auteure questionne les critères de réussite conjugale souvent imposés par l’entourage ou par la société. Les qualités traditionnellement associées au bon époux suffisent-elles à garantir une relation épanouissante ? La question ouvre une réflexion sur la liberté des femmes de définir elles-mêmes leurs attentes et leurs choix. « Il ne suffit pas pour qu’un homme coche toutes les cases, comme on dit, pour être un bon mari. Il ne suffit pas d’être pieux, attentionné, gentil, ou bien avoir de l’argent pour qu’il soit un bon époux », souligne Rokhy Ndiaye. Pour l’auteure, les jeunes femmes doivent pouvoir déterminer leurs propres critères de vie commune, sans se laisser dicter leurs décisions par les normes sociales ou les attentes familiales. Le mariage ne saurait se réduire à une liste de qualités appréciées par l’entourage : il suppose également un choix personnel et une adhésion à la relation. La transmission maternelle occupe, là encore, une place importante. En racontant sa propre histoire à sa fille, la mère cherche à lui faire comprendre qu’elle doit assumer ses décisions. L’héritage des générations précédentes ne consiste donc pas nécessairement à reproduire les mêmes parcours, mais aussi à transmettre la capacité de décider pour soi-même. Les zones d’ombre derrière les apparences Le troisième univers littéraire présenté au cours de la rencontre s’intéresse à la confiance et aux réalités cachées de la vie familiale. L’histoire évoquée met en scène une femme qui pensait connaître parfaitement son mari, avant de découvrir une facette de son passé conjugal dont elle n’avait pas connaissance. Leur fille, Iris, est elle aussi confrontée à une nouvelle lecture de l’histoire de ses parents. Cette découverte bouleverse les certitudes construites au fil des années. Elle rappelle que les relations humaines ne se résument pas toujours aux apparences et que même les personnes les plus proches peuvent conserver des expériences ou des parts de leur histoire que leur entourage ignore. « Donc non, on ne peut pas entièrement connaître une personne », affirme Angelina Uloma Nwachukwu au cours de l’échange. Au-delà de la relation amoureuse, cette réflexion s’étend aux liens familiaux et amicaux. Elle invite à considérer la complexité des individus, dont les attitudes et les décisions peuvent parfois surprendre ceux qui pensent les connaître. Le récit souligne ainsi la difficulté de réduire une personne à une image figée, construite au fil des années. À travers ces récits, le matrimoine se dessine ainsi comme un héritage vivant : celui des paroles, des expériences et des enseignements transmis entre mères et filles, mais aussi celui des questionnements qui permettent aux nouvelles générations de construire leur propre chemin. La littérature devient alors un espace où les histoires individuelles nourrissent une réflexion collective sur les femmes, la famille et la société. Arame NDIAYE

items.title: Les États-Unis imposent des sanctions au ministère rwandais de la Défense et à une institution financière du pays pour des «activités déstabilisatrices» dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo
items.description: Les etats-Unis ont impose des sanctions au ministere rwandais de la Defense et a l'institution financiere specialisee dans les microcredits, Zigama Credit and Savings Society, accusee de soutenir le Mouvement du 23-Mars (M23) dans l'est de la Republique democratique du Congo (RDC), a indique un communique de presse du Departement d'etat americain le 28 octobre. Les troupes rwandaises sont aussi accusees par Washington de soutenir les operations du groupe arme dans les provinces congolaises du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu en fournissant des armes et une formation, et en acheminant « des missiles sol-air et du materiel de brouillage qui mettent en danger l'aviation civile », indique la meme source. Des soupcons de soutien financier, de paiement des achats d'armes et de stockage d'or congolais Washington soupconne Zigama Credit and Savings Society d'avoir facilite, a la demande des autorites rwandaises, les paiements des achats d'armes et d'equipements militaires au profit du M23. Elle est aussi mise en cause pour son role presume dans les transactions financieres liees au M23 et a son aile politique, l'Alliance du fleuve Congo. La societe est par ailleurs accusee d'avoir deplace et stocke des quantites d'or provenant des mines congolaises du Sud-Kivu pour le compte du gouvernement du Rwanda. Les avoirs detenus aux etats-Unis par les deux organismes sanctionnes seront desormais geles et toute transaction en dollars americains leur sera interdite. Des agissements qui sapent « les objectifs de paix et de prosperite des accords de Washington » Le communique de la diplomatie americaine a rappele les objectifs des accords de Washington, censes mettre un terme au conflit et developper le commerce et les investissements dans la region des Grands Lacs en Afrique. Par son soutien au M23, le ministere rwandais de la Defense « viole ces obligations et sape les objectifs de paix et de prosperite des accords de Washington », indique le Departement d'etat, appelant dans la foulee le Rwanda a cesser son soutien au M23 et a « tout groupe arme qui lui succederait », et a retirer ses forces de l'est de la RDC. En matiere d'exploitation miniere, les etats-Unis ont appele les groupes armes et les etats qui les soutiennent a ne pas tirer profit des ressources de la RDC. Ils ont aussi pointe le travail force et les conditions de travail dangereuses des civils dans les zones d'exploitation miniere de l'or et du coltan controlees par le M23, notamment a Rubaya, dans le Nord-Kivu. Dans ce volet, le Departement d'etat a exhorte les partenaires des etats-Unis et le secteur prive a examiner de pres leurs chaînes d'approvisionnement. Les initiatives diplomatiques de Doha et de Washington ne sont pas parvenues a mettre fin au conflit qui sevit toujours dans l'est de la RDC. La signature des accords de Washington, le 4 decembre 2025, par le president congolais Felix Tshisekedi et son homologue rwandais Paul Kagame, n'a pas fait taire les armes ni apporte la stabilite esperee dans la region des Grands Lacs.
