items.title: Meet Nigerian Engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi behind machine that braids hair five times faster
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian-born engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi is gaining attention for developing HaloBraid, an automated hair braiding device designed to help professional stylists complete hairstyles up to five times faster while reducing the physical strain associated with hours of braiding. Ogunbiyi, a Harvard graduate and biomechanical engineer, recently demonstrated how the technology works, offering a glimpse into how automation could transform the hair and beauty industry, particularly protective hairstyles that often require several hours to complete. Unlike a machine that replaces the stylist entirely, HaloBraid is designed to work alongside professional hairdressers. The stylist first sections the hair, applies the necessary products and starts the braid by hand before feeding it into the device. The machine then handles the repetitive weaving along the length of the hair, allowing the stylist to finish and seal the ends. The innovation aims to reduce the time spent on braiding while easing the physical demands placed on stylists who spend long hours working with clients. It also seeks to improve the salon experience without removing the human skill involved in creating the final hairstyle. Ogunbiyi said the inspiration for the invention came from her personal experience of getting her hair braided from childhood and the challenges she repeatedly observed among both stylists and clients. “My braid story starts at age four, sitting between my mum’s legs as she braided my hair for the first time. Since then, I’ve spent thousands of hours getting my hair braided — and heard the same story from stylists and clients again and again: braiding is beautiful, but it takes too much time and too much strain,” she said. Drawing on her background in biomechanical engineering, Ogunbiyi said she recognised the need for a better approach and developed HaloBraid in collaboration with hairstylists, designers and other professionals. She added that the device was built with people close to her in mind, including her mother, hairstylists and aunties, as well as others around the world who understand the experience of spending hours in a salon chair. The venture has also attracted significant investor interest, securing $7 million in seed funding in a round led by Seven Seven Six, the venture capital firm founded by Reddit co founder Alexis Ohanian, who is married to tennis champion Serena Williams. The development adds to Ogunbiyi’s growing recognition in innovation and entrepreneurship. Her HaloBraid project previously won a $75,000 Harvard Innovation Prize, highlighting the potential of the technology to address a familiar challenge in the beauty industry. With its latest demonstration, HaloBraid is positioning itself as a technology that combines traditional hairstyling expertise with automation, potentially giving stylists more time to serve clients while reducing the repetitive work involved in braiding. The post Meet Nigerian Engineer Yinka Ogunbiyi behind machine that braids hair five times faster appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: US Health Secretary RFK Jr to expand access to unapproved peptides
items.description: US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr. has released plans to loosen restrictions on controversial peptides. The plans, which were announced in the US Federal Register on Wednesday, say Kennedy would allow compounding pharmacies to prepare six popular peptides, which not been approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). In an unusual move, the draft came from the office of the health secretary rather than the FDA. After the plan has been officially published later this week, there will be a two-week public comment period. Unregulated injectable peptides have become popular online. Experts have warned of their lack of clinical trials for humans and unknown long-term effects. The peptides mentioned in the plan include BPC-157, TB-500, KPV, MOTS-c and Semax. Compounding pharmacies will be able to mix them to create medications. The BBC has contacted the FDA for comment. An FDA advisory panel voted in July to loosen restrictions on the six peptides. But FDA staff members recommended against it. Kennedy has described himself as a “big fan” of the drugs and has previously vowed to ease restrictions on them after the Biden administration clamped down on the growing industry. Peptides are short chains of amino acids, or small proteins, which our bodies naturally produce. They act as messengers, telling cells what to do, and play vital roles in skin health, immune system and hormone regulation. Peptides have been used to treat medical conditions for more than a century. Insulin, one of the first peptide hormones to be discovered, helps people with Type 1 diabetes and some with Type 2 manage their blood sugar levels. But now unregulated peptides have exploded onto the wellness market since GLP-1s, weight loss drugs, became mainstream. Online influencers have been marketing peptides in what they have called “stacks” for unproven uses, claiming they can be used as a quick way to help people look younger, heal or improve their skin. They have become popular among teens on TikTok, especially boys, over unproven claims they help to build muscle, part of online trends known as “biohacking” and “looksmaxxing”. Health experts have cautioned against use of the drugs, citing a lack of clinical trials for humans and the unknown long-term effects of the substances.

items.title: ATC sentences Imaan, Hadi to 10 years in security breach case
items.description: ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court on Thursday sentenced human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, to 10 years in prison each in the security breach case. Imaan and Hadi were being tried in jail in the 2024 case pertaining to the alleged disruption of an international cricket team’s security route and incitement to public unrest. The couple, accused of removing barriers from the route, was indicted on Oct 7. A formal trial commenced after both lawyers pleaded not guilty. Both were on bail in this case prior to the verdict. Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra announced the verdict in the case at Adiala jail on Thursday, where the trial was conducted. The sentence was handed down under three separate legal provisions. According to the judgment, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the two were sentenced to ten years along with a fine of Rs100,000 each under Section 7 (h) of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, as defined under Section 6 (2) (m) — serious coercion or intimidation of a public servant in order to force him to discharge or to refrain from discharging his lawful duties. The court further handed down a one-year sentence and fined Rs50,000 each under Section 186 (obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). Imaan and Hadi were also sentenced to two years each under Section 353 (assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty) of the PPC. All the sentences will run concurrently, the judgment stated. Justice Sipra held that the two were “jointly responsible for the offence committed under joint object and common intention”. He stated that the objective of the accused was to “compromise the security arrangements through pressuring security officials”. While the court acknowledged that the right of movement was a constitutional right, it held that the “same right is subject to observance of the law of the land, and nobody is allowed to attack/assault” law enforcement agencies. The judgment, citing the attack on the Sri Lankan cricket team in Lahore in 2009, stated that the assault on police personnel and the attempt to “put the security of an international team visiting Pakistan at risk clearly shows the intentions and objective of the accused to create sense of terror”. The court maintained that the two were well-educated persons “having the full knowledge of delicacy of the matter, but they assaulted upon the police officials deputed [there] for ensuring [..] security”. Meanwhile, on charges under Section 506 ii (punishment for criminal intimidation), 120-B (punishment of criminal conspiracy), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), and 149 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object) of the PPC, both Imaan and Hadi were acquitted. The court had appointed a state counsel for the defence in the case. State counsel Atif Mehmood conducted the cross-examination of the witnesses during the trial, while the prosecution presented a total of seven witnesses. On Oct 27, both accused recorded their statements under Section 342 (power to examine the accused) of the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), while final arguments by the state counsel also concluded during the proceedings. On Monday, the couple approached the SC to challenge the IHC’s Oct 19 order refusing to stay the trial in the case. The IHC had heard their appeals last week against an Oct 10 ATC order dismissing petitions challenging the framing of charges and the inclusion of terrorism-related provisions. The high court issued notices and said it would decide how to proceed after receiving responses from the parties. ‘Prisoners of conscience’ In their statements recorded under Section 342 of the CrPC, Imaan and Hadi had denied the charges and alleged that they were being targeted for their human rights work and provision of pro bono legal assistance and services to the marginalised and oppressed communities. “The evidence produced during this trial is not against us, but in fact a charge sheet against (prosecution witnesses)/police officials and the state,” Imaan and Hadi said in their separate similar recorded statements available with Dawn. “I am a prisoner of conscience who has been at the receiving end of state persecution,” the statements read. Imaan pointed out that the entire jail trial had been challenged by the couple in the IHC as well as the SC. Further, the trial was conducted with Imaan and her husband being presented in a cage, preventing effective communication with their counsel or the court, she said. “From day one, our constitutional rights to fair trial, due process and basic human dignity have been infringed,” she stated. She also noted that the couple had been incarcerated for over nine months and handed 17-year sentences a day after their arrest on January 23. “We are being made an example to further cement the chilling effect against those who stand (or want to stand) against tyranny, oppression and injustice,” Imaan stated. The lawyer further highlighted that the two had spent the third year of their marriage in jail and thus “suffered painful separation from one another” very early on. “We have not done so for any personal gain; in fact, we have endured only hardship for our work (and) activism,” she said. “But we surrender ourselves before the ultimate court where we all must return one day, where all will be held accountable for what they have done.” Jailed, sentenced, re-arrested The couple has been in jail since their arrest on Jan 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial. Just a day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act in the controversial social media posts case. The convictions were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts . On September 17, following months of litigation before the courts , the SC suspended their sentences in the case. The SC ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict on their appeals against the trial court’s decision. However, the reprieve was short-lived as hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with the security breach case. The case was registered at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station on March 22 last year on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

items.title: Explorco reports improved 2025 performance ahead of Voltaian Basin drilling
items.description: GNPC Exploration and Production Limited (Explorco) says its financial position improved in 2025 as it prepares for an onshore drilling campaign in the Voltaian Basin in the fourth quarter of 2026. The company reported growth in revenue and profitability, stronger cash generation and a significant reduction in overall borrowings, according to its Managing Director, Samuel Opoku Arthur. He disclosed this at Explorco’s first Annual General Meeting (AGM), held at the Accra Marriott Hotel on Tuesday, October 27, 2026. Mr Arthur said the improved performance provided a stronger financial foundation for future investments, although the company continued to manage outstanding financial obligations and receivables. He also outlined operational progress across assets in the Jubilee and Tweneboa, Enyenra and Ntomme (TEN) fields, as well as preparations to ensure readiness for the Voltaian Basin drilling campaign. Explorco’s Board Chairman, Dr Aaron Issa Anafure, said the company’s transition to direct operatorship would require strong technical expertise, disciplined project management, sound procurement practices and effective risk management. He stressed that safety, accountability and stakeholder trust would be critical to building a credible Ghanaian operator. Dr Anafure also described the Voltaian Basin project as an opportunity to strengthen national capacity and develop expertise that could shape the future of Ghana’s upstream petroleum industry. Deputy Minister for Energy and Green Transition Richard Gyan-Mensah said the government expected the company to meet its commitments, including commencing the onshore drilling campaign as scheduled in the fourth quarter of 2026. He urged Explorco’s leadership to maintain due process and conduct rigorous due diligence throughout the project’s execution. The meeting brought together board members, executives of parent company Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC), government officials and industry stakeholders. Those present included Mr Gyan-Mensah, Dr Anafure, Mr Opoku Arthur and GNPC Chief Executive Officer Kwame Ntow Amoah. Representatives of the Ministry of Energy and Green Transition, GNPC subsidiaries—including Ghana National Gas Company Limited, Prestea Sankofa Gold Limited and Mole Motel Company Limited—and external auditors Deloitte Ghana also attended. Explorco is GNPC’s upstream operating subsidiary, responsible for oil and gas exploration and production in Ghana. At the inaugural AGM, the company reaffirmed its commitment to improving operational efficiency, strengthening local content participation and maintaining high safety standards as it works towards becoming a fully capable and financially disciplined operator. The planned Voltaian Basin drilling campaign is expected to be a key test of the company’s operational readiness and its ambition to expand Ghanaian participation in upstream petroleum operations.

items.title: Coopération militaire: ouverture de la deuxième session de Comité mixte de suivi Burkina Faso-Egypte
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 27 octobre 2026) – Le Ministère de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique (MGDP) a abrité, ce 27 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie d’ouverture de la deuxième session du Comité mixte de suivi de la coopération militaire et technique entre la République arabe d’Égypte et le Burkina Faso. Prévus sur deux jours, les travaux ont été ouverts par le Camarade Secrétaire Général du MGDP, l’Intendant Colonel-Major Yamba Léonard OUOBA. Conformément au protocole de coopération qui lie les deux pays, le Comité mixte de suivi se réunit tous les deux ans. À la suite de la première session, tenue au Caire du 12 au 15 octobre 2024, le Burkina Faso a l’honneur d’accueillir cette deuxième session, qui permettra de dresser le bilan des acquis enregistrés au cours des deux dernières années. Dans son allocution d’ouverture, le Camarade Secrétaire Général a souhaité la bienvenue à la délégation égyptienne, conduite par le Général de Brigade Tawfik Mostafa Tawfik El Said. Il a salué le Burkina Faso, « pays des Hommes intègres, terre d’hospitalité », où les hôtes égyptiens se trouvent chez eux, parmi des frères d’armes. Au titre d’un programme de travail ambitieux, les deux délégations examineront l’état de mise en œuvre des activités retenues lors de la première session, procéderont à des échanges sur le Plan de coopération 2027-2028 et aborderont divers points relatifs à l’Accord. Évoquant un contexte régional et international marqué par des défis sécuritaires multiformes, l’Intendant Colonel-Major OUOBA a rappelé que cette coopération repose sur le respect mutuel, la souveraineté des États et la recherche d’intérêts partagés. Il a invité les participants à conduire les travaux dans un esprit de franchise et de fraternité, au bénéfice des deux pays et de leurs armées respectives. Il a exprimé sa gratitude aux participants pour leur présence et leur engagement. Il a enfin formulé ses vœux de plein succès aux travaux, et souhaité une coopération militaire fructueuse entre le Burkina Faso et la République arabe d’Égypte. DCRP/MGDP L’article Coopération militaire: ouverture de la deuxième session de Comité mixte de suivi Burkina Faso-Egypte est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Fire destroys restaurant, make-up shop and boutique at Goaso
items.description: A fire outbreak has completely destroyed a restaurant, a make-up shop and a boutique housed in a wooden structure at Goaso in the Ahafo Region. The incident occurred on Sunday, October 25, prompting an emergency response from personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) at the Goaso Municipal Fire Station. According to the GNFS, firefighters responded to the incident at about 11:35 am and arrived to find the three businesses engulfed in flames. The crew swiftly deployed hose lines to contain the blaze and prevent it from spreading to adjoining properties. The fire was brought under control at 12:18 pm and completely extinguished at 1:09 pm. Despite the timely intervention, the restaurant, make-up shop and boutique, together with their contents, were completely destroyed. However, the GNFS indicated that the response of firefighters prevented further destruction to nearby properties. The Ahafo Regional Fire Commander, Assistant Chief Fire Officer Grade II (ACFO II) Samuel Ferdie Tetteh, accompanied by the Operations Commander, Assistant Divisional Officer Grade I (ADO I) Samuel Afram, subsequently visited the scene to assess the extent of the damage. The cause of the fire remains unknown, with investigations underway to establish the circumstances surrounding the outbreak.

items.description: L’AS Douanes organise, les 29 et 30 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une session de formation consacrée à la gouvernance, à la planification stratégique et opérationnelle ainsi qu’à la gestion de ses sections sportives. À travers cette initiative, le club omnisports entend renforcer ses capacités organisationnelles, diversifier ses ressources et consolider ses ambitions sur les scènes nationale et internationale. La session s’est ouverte ce jeudi 29 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou avec l’accompagnement technique de Global Sport Management (GSM). L’AS Douanes veut franchir un nouveau cap dans son développement. Au-delà des performances enregistrées sur les terrains, le club mise désormais sur une gouvernance plus efficace et une gestion mieux structurée de ses différentes disciplines. C’est dans cette dynamique que s’inscrit la présente session de formation. Durant deux jours, les responsables du Bureau exécutif et des sections sportives vont travailler sur les mécanismes de gouvernance, la planification des activités, la budgétisation, la mobilisation des ressources et le suivi-évaluation. L’objectif est de doter les dirigeants d’outils adaptés pour améliorer le fonctionnement de l’association et assurer la pérennité de ses acquis. Le président du Bureau exécutif de l’AS Douanes, l’Inspecteur Divisionnaire des Douanes Moumouni Derra, a souligné l’importance de cette rencontre pour l’avenir du club. Selon lui, l’association se trouve à un tournant décisif, marqué par des ambitions sportives, institutionnelles et économiques croissantes. Au fil des saisons, l’AS Douanes s’est affirmée comme un acteur du mouvement sportif burkinabè. Les performances réalisées au cours de la saison 2025-2026 dans ses six disciplines, notamment le football, le basketball, le volleyball, le handball, le judo et l’athlétisme, témoignent du travail accompli par les dirigeants, les encadreurs et les athlètes. Toutefois, ces succès ne doivent pas occulter les difficultés auxquelles l’association reste confrontée, en particulier la faiblesse et l’insuffisante diversification de ses sources de financement. Face à ces contraintes, le président du Bureau exécutif estime nécessaire d’adopter une gestion plus rigoureuse. « Un grand club ne se construit pas uniquement sur les terrains de compétition », Inspecteur Divisionnaire des Douanes Moumouni Derra « Un grand club ne se construit pas uniquement sur les terrains de compétition. Il se forge d’abord dans la qualité de sa gouvernance et la pertinence de ses choix stratégiques », a-t-il déclaré. Pour Moumouni Derra l’enjeu est donc de dépasser une gestion dictée par les urgences pour privilégier l’anticipation, la programmation et la recherche de résultats mesurables. Partenaire technique de cette initiative, Global Sport Management entend accompagner l’AS Douanes dans la construction d’une organisation plus moderne et performante. Pour son responsable, Moussa René Sanou, l’élaboration d’un plan stratégique doit s’accompagner d’une planification opérationnelle impliquant aussi bien le Bureau exécutif que les différentes sections sportives. « Il ne s’agira pas pour Global Sport de venir donner des cours académiques. Il s’agira effectivement pour Global Sport d’apprendre aussi de l’AS Douanes et de voir les préoccupations majeures des acteurs » , a expliqué Moussa René Sanou. À travers cette session, l’AS Douanes entend ainsi faire de la qualité de sa gouvernance un levier essentiel de développement. Pour Moumouni Derra, la réussite du projet repose sur la solidarité, la discipline et la victoire, les trois valeurs inscrites dans la devise du club. Une victoire qui ne se limite pas aux trophées, mais englobe aussi la modernisation des structures et la construction d’un avenir durable pour l’association. items.title: Bilawal urges Achakzai to use ‘authority’ delegated by Imran, asks opposition to play role in Parliament
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday urged National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai to use the “authority and power” delegated to him by jailed PTI founder Imran Khan to direct opposition members to participate in House committees and discuss pressing national issues. He made the remarks while addressing the National Assembly during a session chaired by Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa. Addressing the House, Bilawal called for strengthening Parliament by taking decisions on matters of national interest collectively on a single platform. “If Parliament is powerful, we are all powerful; this is the power bestowed on us by the people of Pakistan,” he said. Urging the speaker and the government to fulfil their responsibilities, the PPP chairman also called on the opposition to play its role in the House. “Those who want this House to remain dysfunctional and do not want the people of Pakistan to benefit from it have succeeded,” he said, pointing towards the opposition benches. “Congratulations to you,” he added sarcastically. “You have played a part in helping these people achieve their objective,” he said, criticising the opposition. Bilawal also criticised the opposition’s decision to boycott committee proceedings, saying it had contributed to the “weakening” of Parliament. “It is your responsibility to represent your party, the people and your constituencies in these committees. However, you are not raising their concerns on the relevant platforms,” he said. Turning to Achakzai, Bilawal urged the opposition leader to use the “authority and power” delegated to him and the Senate opposition leader by Imran Khan to direct opposition members to participate in committee proceedings and discuss pressing national issues. Bilawal said that since Parliament had decided, on a motion moved by the PPP, to constitute a committee on electoral reforms, the opposition leader should nominate a representative to the committee and submit the name to the speaker’s office. He recalled that the opposition had described electoral rigging as its “fundamental issue”. Urging the opposition leader to participate in the committee’s proceedings, Bilawal said the move was necessary if the opposition wanted the issue of alleged rigging to be addressed before the next general election, local government polls or by-elections. The PPP chairman also described participation in the committee as a fundamental step towards restoring Parliament’s respect and authority. “I request the opposition to at least exercise the power it has,” he said, questioning the purpose of an electoral reforms committee if the opposition did not participate in its proceedings. “If we make efforts to bring all stakeholders together in a committee or arrange a briefing on terrorism, economic and security issues, and other concerns without the opposition’s participation, it will be pointless,” he said. Against the backdrop of the evolving geopolitical situation, Bilawal called for the foreign, interior and defence ministers to brief the House on the challenges facing Pakistan. “Tell this House about the potential threats facing Pakistan and the region, particularly as three key maritime routes are closed,” he said. He also called for a briefing on developments related to the war in Iran and its implications for Pakistan. In addition, he sought a briefing from the government on the recent defence pacts signed by Pakistan. “Every member of this House has the right to be informed about the challenges facing Pakistan, whether terrorism or other domestic issues, the steps being taken to address them and their potential consequences in the days ahead,” he said. Addressing a rally in Karachi earlier this month, Bilawal had also extended an olive branch to the opposition parties, saying their positive engagement with the federal government could result in the reversal of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The PPP chairman had invited the opposition to join the Parliamentary electoral reforms process and “engage with the federal government”. The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move had drawn criticism from the opposition. PPP delegation meets Achakzai Separately, a PPP delegation met Achakzai and invited the PTI to join the parliamentary committee on electoral reforms, according to a statement the party issued on X. The PPP delegation comprised of Raja Pervez Ashraf and Syed Naveed Qamar. Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas was also present. The delegation invited Achakzai to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms, the statement said. Later, in a press conference, Ashraf said the PPP delegation had a meeting with Achakzai on Bilawal’s instructions to invite him to join the committee. “The PPP wants the PTI to participate in parliamentary standing committees as well as the electoral reforms committee,” he added. Achakzai had sought time to consult before responding to the invitation, he said. The PPP has consistently sought to improve the electoral process, Ashraf said, adding that PTI also wanted electoral reforms. “The PTI will respond to the PPP after consultations,” he said.

items.title: L’œil de Guinéenews : Le fléau des vieux véhicules polluants en circulation
items.description: Voir un véhicule, fatigué ou vieux, qui crache une épaisse fumée blanche par son pot d'échappement est une image assez courante, certes, mais avouons-le, elle est source de tristesse. Cette émanation opaque aveugle et asphyxie les automobilistes et les motocyclistes. Elle enveloppe aussi les piétons dans un nuage qui les étouffe et les fait suffoquer, transformant leur course, en une véritable épreuve de respiration. Mais, quelle est la cause de ce phénomène ? Une fumée blanche et épaisse qui sort d'un pot d'échappement (particulièrement sur un véhicule diesel) traduit généralement un dysfonctionnement mécanique important. Mais, faisons plutôt simple, comme nous ne sommes pas dans un exposé de mécanique générale. La sortie de la fumée blanche peut être due à une fuite de liquide de refroidissement, à un problème d'injection ou de combustion ou à l'usure générale du moteur. Il s'agit là, de données techniques qui ne sont pas accessibles à tous les lecteurs. Aussi, voudront-ils, s'ils désirent mieux comprendre les termes usités, en référer à leur mécanicien ou à un spécialiste du domaine. Quelles sont les conséquences de ces gaz sur les personnes, la circulation et la sécurité routière ? L'inhalation pendant un certain temps, de ces gaz et fumées, provoque des irritations aiguës des yeux, du nez et de la gorge, ainsi que des quintes de toux. Cela peut même être plus grave, pour ceux-là qui souffrent d’asthme ou de problèmes respiratoires. Ajoutons également le fait que la visibilité des conducteurs est fortement réduite, lorsque la fumée est épaisse. En même temps, les risques d'accidents de la circulation s’accroissent nettement, tant pour ceux qui roulent, juste derrière un autre, que pour ceux qui se croisent ou se dépassent. C’est alors que les chocs par arrière, les collisions et les accrochages se multiplient. Conséquences sur l'environnement Il n’y a pas que les individus seuls, pris isolément, qui pâtissent de cette situation très dommageable pour la santé publique . Nous sommes là, confrontés à une véritable pollution atmosphérique . Ces rejets massifs contribuent lourdement à la dégradation de la qualité de l'air urbain. Ils forment, comme un brouillard toxique, invisible à l’œil nu, mais nocif pour tous les riverains. Et les conséquences sont même plus étendues. Ce phénomène est en lien direct avec le climat que nous vivons. Tous ces véhicules en fin de vie ou mal réglés, participent activement à la pollution environnementale et au réchauffement climatique, par l’émission constante de particules fines et de gaz à effet de serre. C’est pourquoi, le contrôle technique est absolument nécessaire et doit être scrupuleusement respecté. On accepte encore chez nous que des épaves roulantes roulent dans les agglomérations ou en rase campagne. Mais, nous risquons de payer lourdement cette tolérance, car au-delà de l’inconfort olfactif et visuel qui nous choquent, c'est toute la chaîne de la sécurité sanitaire et environnementale urbaine qui est mise à mal. Et nous risquons de le payer très cher, surtout sur le long terme.

items.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, les neuf doigts de Lula et la banalisation du mépris du handicap en politique (Par Mamour Sop Ndiaye)
items.description: Le Brésil vient de vivre l’une des élections présidentielles les plus disputées et les plus imprévisibles de son histoire. Le 25 octobre 2026, plus de 128 millions de Brésiliens se sont rendus aux urnes pour départager Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80 ans, et Flávio Bolsonaro, 45 ans, fils de l’ancien président. Arrivé deuxième au premier tour (45,16 % contre 47,03 %), Lula a renversé le résultat au second, obtenant 51,79 % des suffrages. Une victoire historique, au terme d’une campagne marquée par des attaques personnelles révélatrices de certains préjugés envers la vieillesse et le handicap. Neuf doigts et quatre-vingts ans : la dérision comme arme politique Lors du dernier débat télévisé, le 23 octobre, Flávio Bolsonaro a ironisé sur les « neuf doigts » de Lula, provoquant des rires dans une partie du public. Cette formule renvoyait à un accident du travail survenu en 1964, lorsque Lula, âgé de 17 ans, perdit l’auriculaire de sa main gauche dans une usine métallurgique de São Paulo. Indigné, Lula rappela les circonstances de cet accident et exigea des excuses. Le candidat a également affirmé avoir du mal à comprendre les propos de Lula, tournant en dérision sa voix enrouée. Or, l’ancien métallurgiste a été traité pour un cancer du larynx en 2011, avant de subir, en 2022, une intervention chirurgicale pour retirer une lésion bénigne d’une corde vocale. Durant cette campagne particulièrement intense, sa voix était de nouveau éprouvée. Ces remarques ont ainsi été perçues comme des allusions dévalorisantes à la vieillesse et aux fragilités physiques. Mais ce face-à-face n’opposait pas simplement deux générations. D’un côté, un ancien ouvrier devenu dirigeant syndical, trois fois président de la République avant ce scrutin, dont la biographie traverse plus d’un demi-siècle de luttes sociales et politiques. De l’autre, un héritier politique de 45 ans, entré au Parlement régional à 21 ans, sans avoir connu la condition ouvrière ni les risques industriels auxquels son adversaire fut exposé dès l’adolescence. La réponse des Brésiliens : des aînés portés jusqu’aux urnes Deux jours plus tard, le Brésil découvrait des images bouleversantes. Des enfants portaient leurs parents, des petits-enfants soutenaient leurs grands-parents ; des personnes très âgées ou handicapées arrivaient en fauteuil roulant, avec une canne, un déambulateur, parfois même sur un brancard. Certaines devaient être soulevées dans les bras de leurs proches pour franchir les escaliers des bureaux de vote. Plusieurs affichaient leur soutien à Lula. Ces scènes ont pris, aux yeux de nombreux Brésiliens, la dimension d’une réponse symbolique aux attaques contre l’âge et les différences physiques. Sans prétendre que tous ces électeurs partageaient les mêmes motivations, leur détermination demeure remarquable dans un pays où le vote est facultatif après 70 ans. Le 27 octobre, jour de son 81e anniversaire, Lula n’a pu retenir ses larmes en évoquant ces images de personnes âgées transportées dans les bras de leurs enfants et petits-enfants pour exercer leur droit de vote. Cette solidarité admirable rappelle aussi les obstacles que rencontrent encore les personnes âgées et handicapées dans l’exercice de leur citoyenneté. Les familles ne devraient pas avoir à pallier les insuffisances d’accessibilité des bureaux de vote. Au terme de cette élection, deux images restent gravées dans les mémoires : la main d’un ancien ouvrier privée d’un doigt par le travail, et les bras de familles portant leurs aînés vers les urnes. Deux images qui nous interrogent sur le respect dû aux travailleurs, aux personnes handicapées et à nos anciens. Dr Mamour Sop Ndiaye – Enseignant-chercheur et chef du Département de Génie Électrique au CEFET/RJ, Brésil. Docteur en ingénierie électrique, spécialiste en planification, transition et efficacité énergétiques.

items.title: Ajax Amsterdam : Abdellah Ouazane confirme tout son potentiel
items.description: Annoncé tout proche du Real Madrid avant que son transfert ne capote à la suite d’un problème détecté lors de la visite médicale, Abdellah Ouazane est en train de s’imposer à l’Ajax Amsterdam. À seulement 17 ans, le jeune international marocain affiche déjà des statistiques prometteuses et poursuit son ascension en Eredivisie. L’échec de son transfert au Real Madrid aurait pu freiner sa progression. Il semble finalement avoir constitué un nouveau départ pour Abdellah Ouazane. Resté à l’Ajax Amsterdam, son club formateur, le jeune milieu offensif marocain profite de la confiance accordée aux jeunes talents pour découvrir rapidement le football professionnel. Un an après avoir été annoncé tout proche du géant espagnol, le joueur de 17 ans commence à se faire une place dans l’effectif amstellodamois. Son transfert à Madrid avait échoué au dernier moment à la suite d’un problème détecté lors de la visite médicale, alors qu’il sortait d’une Coupe d’Afrique des nations U17 particulièrement réussie avec le Maroc, compétition au cours de laquelle il avait été élu meilleur joueur. Loin de se laisser abattre par cet épisode, Ouazane affirme en avoir tiré une motivation supplémentaire. « J’en ai justement tiré de la force. Revenir à l’Ajax était ma meilleure option », expliquait-il, déterminé à démontrer l’étendue de son potentiel. Le jeune Marocain affiche un bilan encourageant depuis le début de la saison. Selon les chiffres rapportés par Foot Mercato, il totalise trois buts et trois passes décisives en 17 rencontres toutes compétitions confondues. En quelques mois, le joueur est ainsi passé d’un transfert avorté au Real Madrid à une présence dans la rotation d’un club historique du football européen et à une première expérience avec les A du Maroc. L’Ajax mise sur son potentiel L’entraîneur de l’Ajax, Míchel, reconnaît les qualités du jeune Marocain, tout en soulignant les axes de progression qui lui restent à travailler. « Il doit encore progresser, oui. Il doit gagner en régularité pendant les matchs. Il s’entraîne bien pour y parvenir. Le talent est là. Il est très talentueux » , a-t-il déclaré en conférence de presse. À 17 ans, Abdellah Ouazane doit encore gagner en constance et poursuivre son adaptation aux exigences du haut niveau. Mais son début de parcours professionnel et sa progression internationale témoignent déjà du potentiel qui avait attiré l’attention du Real Madrid. The post Ajax Amsterdam : Abdellah Ouazane confirme tout son potentiel appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Mr Agbodza also highlighted the importance of partnerships with international institutions and development partners in mobilising investment, technical expertise and other resources to support Ghana’s infrastructure priorities. items.title: Édouard Philippe, candidat à la présidentielle française, ressort le « bras de fer » avec l’Algérie
items.description: Pas sûr d'accéder au second tour, le candidat du centre à l'élection présidentielle française de 2027, Édouard Philippe , actionne le levier de l’Algérie et de l’immigration et fait de la surenchère. Constat d' « échec de l'intégration depuis plusieurs décennies », « surreprésentation » des jeunes issus de l’immigration lors des dernières émeutes qui ont secoué la France samedi 17 octobre, promesse de réduire l’immigration légale de moitié, de restreindre le regroupement familial et de dénoncer l'accord franco-algérien de 1968 sur l’immigration. Dans une interview au Point, l’ancien Premier ministre d’Emmanuel Macron a tenu des propos difficiles à distinguer de la rhétorique de l’extrême-droite. Immigration en France : pour Édouard Philippe, l'échec de l’intégration est “ incontestable ” “ Lors des violences du 17 octobre, la surreprésentation de jeunes issus de l'immigration était patente. (…) L'échec de l'intégration dans notre pays depuis plusieurs décennies est incontestable ”, a déclaré le chef du parti Horizons. Et voici ce qu'il promet de faire s’il est élu au printemps prochain concernant l’immigration : “Je veux, au cours du prochain quinquennat, diviser l'immigration légale par deux en limitant la délivrance de titres de séjour aux seuls motifs professionnels et aux étudiants, restreindre le regroupement familial, réformer l'instruction de l'asile ”. Édouard Philippe promet de durcir le “ bras de fer ” avec l’Algérie Édouard Philippe n'oublie pas l’Algérie, devenue objet de surenchère électorale d’une large frange de la classe politique française. Le candidat a promis de “ durcir le bras de fer avec les pays d'origine (de l’immigration, ndlr), et notamment avec l'Algérie en dénonçant le traité de 1968 ”. Philippe était l'un des tout premiers à soutenir l’idée de révocation de l'accord de 1968 lancée en 2023 par Xavier Driencourt, ancien ambassadeur en Algérie. Imane Bounouh répond à Édouard Philippe : “ On ne sera pas le cache-nez de votre xénophobie ” Imane Bounouh, élue municipale de gauche au Mans, a répondu à Édouard Philippe sur Instagram. “ Il dit en parlant des jeunes du 17 octobre que c’est le signe de l'échec de l’intégration. Là où nous, on voit des Français, lui il voit des Noirs et des Arabes ”, a dit l'élue et influenceuse d'origine algérienne et marocaine. Dans l’interview, Philippe a indiqué que l’échec de l’intégration “ ne minimise en aucun cas certaines superbes réussites d'intégration républicaine ”. Pour Imane Bounouh, cette phrase est juste destinée à “ alléger ” le “ propos xénophobe ” du candidat à la présidentielle. “ On n’est pas vos très beaux exemples d’intégration républicaine et on ne sera pas les cautions de votre système qui ne marche pas. Et surtout, on ne sera pas le cache-nez de votre xénophobie et de votre racisme ”, lui a-t-elle rétorqué. Le post d’Imane Bounouh a été partagé sur X par la championne de basket Emilie Gomis. items.title: WAFU B WCL: Ampem Darkoa Ladies beat Edo Queens in final replay to qualify for CAF Women’s Champions League
items.description: Ghana Women’s Premier League champions, Ampem Darkoa Ladies, will play in the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League after beating Edo Queens in the replay of their WAFU B qualifier final. The two teams faced each other to play the extra time of the final after the Confederation of African Football nullified results from the penalty shootouts after they met in Burkina Faso last month. The earlier meeting went straight into penalties after the game had ended 2-2 in 90 minutes, with the Nigerian side winning in the shootouts. However, the Ghanaian side appealed the decision, which was upheld by CAF, ordering a replay of the final with extra time being the focus. During Thursday’s meeting, Ampem Darkoa scored just two minutes into the start of the game from a corner to take the lead and make it 3-2. The Ghanaian side came under constant pressure after going ahead in the game, but Charles Anokye Frimpong’s side held on to their lead to see out the challenge from the Nigerians, eventually sealing the win. The victory sees Ampem Darkoa qualify for the 2026 edition of the CAF Women’s Champions League, which will also be their second appearance in the competition. The Ghanaian champions will face Morocco’s AS FAR, Kawempe Muslim Ladies of Uganda and USFAS Bamako of Mali in the tournament which kicks off on November 1 in Egypt.

items.title: GenCED calls for political-financing reforms over vote-buying allegations
items.description: The Gender Centre for Empowering Development (GenCED) has called for reforms to address alleged vote-buying and financial inducements in Ghana’s political party elections, warning that money politics threatens fair competition and limits the participation of women and young people. In a statement issued on Monday, October 26, the organisation said concerns surrounding the National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency executive elections held on October 24 and the New Patriotic Party (NPP) constituency executive elections held on July 11 and 12 highlight the need to tackle the problem as a national democratic challenge. GenCED said allegations of financial inducements had emerged in contests involving both major political parties, making political-financing reform an issue that should transcend partisan interests. The organisation cited the NPP presidential primaries held on January 31, 2026, and the NDC’s Ayawaso East parliamentary primary on March 3, 2026, which attracted investigations by the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP). “These developments demonstrate why political-financing reform must be a national priority rather than a partisan debate,” the statement said. GenCED said its research, titled The Price to Participate: How Money in Politics Undermines Women and Youth Political Participation in Ghana , highlights how financial demands, patronage networks, campaign expenditure and the informal costs of political participation can restrict access to political leadership. The organisation warned that when financial inducements dominate internal elections, candidates with access to wealthy sponsors and established patronage networks could gain an advantage over those with fewer resources. “When cash and material inducements become instruments of political competition, the ability to mobilise financial resources risks overshadowing leadership capacity, policy ideas, integrity and commitment to public service,” it said. GenCED added that women, young people and persons with disabilities could face additional barriers in an already unequal political environment. To address the concerns, the organisation urged political parties and relevant stakeholders to strengthen preventive measures and enforcement. Its recommendations include voter and delegate education, independent scrutiny of internal elections, impartial investigations and transparent reporting of outcomes. It also called for cross-party dialogue involving political parties, state institutions and civil society organisations to develop practical, evidence-based reforms to protect the integrity of political competition. “These measures must become priorities rather than promises made in response to controversy,” the statement said. GenCED stressed that internal party elections are central to democratic governance because they determine who leads political organisations, represents their members and influences decisions that shape national leadership. It said the credibility of these processes depends on delegates being able to make free choices, candidates competing fairly and complaints being resolved without intimidation or undue financial influence. “Ghana’s democratic future must not be determined by who can spend the most, but by who can lead with integrity, competence, accountability and a genuine commitment to the public good,” the organisation said. The statement comes as political parties continue their internal reorganisation ahead of the 2028 general elections. GenCED said it would continue advocating gender-responsive political-financing reforms and inclusive governance systems to enable all Ghanaians, particularly women and young people, to participate meaningfully in political decision-making.

items.title: Cómo ayudar a las víctimas tras una catástrofe como el accidente de tren de Urda: “El psicólogo debe estar desde el minuto uno, como un bombero”
items.description: Tras vivir una tragedia como el accidente de trenes de Toledo, el mundo de las víctimas se derrumba. Cae la sensación de invulnerabilidad, la convicción de que el mundo es un lugar seguro que podemos controlar. De que, siempre que uno actúe como debe, no ocurrirá nada malo. Esta idea, explican los psicólogos, surge en los primeros años de vida. Es entonces cuando el niño desarrolla un sentido de confianza básica: la percepción de que el mundo es un lugar predecible donde, si uno se comporta bien, todo irá bien. El mundo no funciona así, pero a veces es necesario pensar que sí para poder llevar una vida funcional. Poder coger el coche, el tren o salir a pasear sin pensar que podemos morir en cualquier momento. La recuperación psicológica de las víctimas, en gran medida, pasa por reconstruir dichas suposiciones. Dejar de ver el mundo como un lugar eternamente peligroso y volver a confiar. Seguir leyendo

Polluted priorities
items.description: LAHORE is choking again, and the government’s answer is to send more machines onto its streets. On Wednesday, its air quality index reached 296 , putting children, outdoor workers, and the elderly at particular risk. Yet Punjab plans to acquire 30 more truck-mounted fog cannons. These can suppress road dust locally, but their ability to reduce the fine particles most harmful to health remains questionable. Authorities must explain what the existing fleet has achieved in terms of measurable pollution reduction before spending more public money. Last year, disruptions to Punjab’s air monitoring network raised suspicions that pollution levels were being hidden; officials cited technical faults. Whether equipment is recording pollution or spraying water, public confidence depends on transparent data and independent scrutiny. A temporary improvement at a pollution hotspot, or near a monitoring station, cannot prove that the city’s air is becoming safer. Monitoring should expose pollution. Punjab must publish continuous readings and independent assessments of its interventions. It should also fund research into the relative contributions of traffic, industry, construction, and crop burning, how these change with the seasons, and which measures actually reduce exposure. That scientific effort must extend beyond the border. Punjab officials say easterly winds have been bringing polluted air from India into Lahore. But this does not absolve Pakistan of responsibility for its own emissions. The air over the two Punjabs is shared, and both populations suffer when political hostility obstructs cooperation. Calls for joint action are not new. Cooperation was proposed with Indian Punjab in 2017 and 2024. Yet neither initiative led to sustained cooperation. Environmental diplomacy with New Delhi should be prioritised, despite wider tensions. Both sides could begin by exchanging verified air-quality and weather data, jointly studying the movement of pollutants and developing common approaches to agricultural burning and industrial emissions. Universities and scientific institutions could help build a shared evidence base. At home, dedicated research funding, stronger monitoring, and open evaluation of anti-smog spending are essential. Enforcement must continue, but decisions should follow evidence, not the visibility of machinery on city roads. Until the air itself improves, no amount of official activity can be called progress. Published in Dawn, October 29th, 2026

items.title: 2027: Abia CP warns politicians against violence, intimidation
items.description: …Orders parties to notify police before rallies . We ‘re for nobody, we ‘re for everybody – REC, urges candidates to accept results or seek redress in court By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Afolabi, has warned political parties and their supporters against violence, intimidation, inflammatory statements and destruction of property ahead of the 2027 general elections. This is as the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its neutrality in the 2027 Abia governorship election, assuring all candidates that it will provide a level playing field for every contestant. CP Afolabi, who spoke at the signing of a peace accord involving the NEC, security agencies and political parties in Umuahia, urged parties to notify the police in writing before holding rallies, processions and other political activities to enable adequate security arrangements. The meeting, held at the Police Officers’ Mess, Umuahia, was attended by INEC’s Resident Electoral Commissioner in Abia, Prof. Sylvia Agu, heads of sister security agencies and representatives of registered political parties and campaign teams. The Police boss reaffirmed the command’s commitment to providing professional, impartial and adequate security for all candidates, parties and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation. He disclosed that the command had strengthened its security architecture through intelligence gathering and analysis, crime mapping, the revamp of its Cybercrime Unit and improved operational response mechanisms. Afolabi also acknowledged Governor Alex Otti’s directive on adequate security for political campaigns and related activities. He pledged continued collaboration with INEC, other security agencies and political stakeholders to protect lives and property and ensure a peaceful electoral process. The peace accord, which followed a review of relevant electoral laws by the command’s legal officer, was subsequently read to the stakeholders before representatives of political parties signed individually, pledging to pursue their political ambitions peacefully. Speaking at the event, the REC, Prof. Agu, said the commission was committed to serving all candidates equally, irrespective of their political parties, while urging them to maintain peace before, during and after the election. “We are not working for any particular party; we are working for all of you here. We are going to deliver on our mandate, but we are asking you to conduct yourselves properly,” she said. The REC urged candidates to accept the outcome of a free, fair and credible election, advising those dissatisfied with the results to seek redress through the judiciary rather than resort to violence or discredit the electoral process. She stressed that electoral contests inevitably produce winners and losers, urging candidates to demonstrate sportsmanship regardless of the outcome. “In any contest, there must be a winner and a loser. If you win, we thank God and rejoice with you. If you lose, you can try again next time,” Agu said. She added that the peace accord was designed to prevent violence and conflict by committing all signatories to peaceful conduct throughout the electoral process. The signing brought together governorship candidates, INEC officials, police representatives and other security agencies as stakeholders sought a peaceful atmosphere for the 2027 polls. items.title: VIDEO: Titus Glover pours libation over La Pleasure Beach demolition
items.description: Former Greater Accra Regional Minister Titus Glover has poured libation, calling on traditional deities to intervene in the demolition of structures at La Pleasure Beach, which has affected businesses and livelihoods. The act took place during the Ga-Dangme Progressive Front’s demonstration, dubbed “Aaagbe wɔ demo,” organised to protest the demolitions and draw attention to concerns over the impact on affected residents and businesses. The National Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) appeal to the gods added a traditional dimension to the protest, as demonstrators raised concerns about the destruction of structures and the disruption of livelihoods at the beach. The demonstration forms part of growing calls for attention to the concerns of communities affected by demolitions in parts of Greater Accra. The demonstration follows calls by the Coalition of La Associations (COLA) to the government and relevant authorities in seven days to respond to demands for compensation for businesses and traders affected by the demolition exercises at Laboma Beach Resort and La Pleasure Beach. The Coalition warned that failure to address the concerns could result in lawful protests, petitions to the Presidency and Parliament, and possible legal action. The Coalition recalled that on September 13, 2026, the government’s Post-Flood Mitigation Task Force demolished structures at Laboma Beach Resort as part of efforts to restore the Kpeshie Lagoon and reduce flooding. Another demolition exercise followed on October 2, 2026, at La Pleasure Beach and adjoining areas, affecting restaurants, bars and other commercial establishments. Citing figures from the Ghana Tourism Federation, COLA said 85 businesses were affected at La Pleasure Beach alone, putting approximately 4,000 jobs at risk, with women accounting for a significant proportion of the affected workers.

items.title: Can Democracy Survive the Next Financial Crash?
items.description: T he bailout clock is ticking. In September, Oracle invoked “force majeure” to delay paying debt on a data center, which led to a drop in the corporation’s stock price. This month, OpenAI significantly cut its revenue projections; CoreWeave, a heavily leveraged data-center company, saw its share price plunge; and investors began racing to buy credit-default swaps to protect their portfolios. These are all signs of declining investor confidence. The risk that the heavily debt-fueled and interconnected AI sector could crash—taking the broader economy with it—is high and rising. When the next crash happens, originating from whatever sector, the president will control a bailout apparatus with essentially limitless authority. Ever since the 2008 global financial crisis, the Federal Reserve and U.S. Treasury have claimed, with almost no resistance, more power to deal with each successive financial emergency. These bailouts were rationalized on the basis that they were in the public interest and at least theoretically subject to congressional oversight. But if the crash happens on Donald Trump’s watch , his administration would likely sidestep Congress entirely. A Trump bailout would proceed on whatever terms please the president and his allies, who would use it as a bonanza to enrich their favored companies and CEOs, even if they were the ones who caused the crisis to begin with. The billionaires—and the trillionaire—in Trump’s inner circle have already usurped decision making about which federal agencies to decimate, which federal workers to fire, which scientific research to defund, and which industries to deem necessary for national security. They could also usurp the bailout apparatus, making it spin into action even before a crisis arrives. When they start feeling financially wobbly, they might go to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh, or, most likely, Trump himself and request an emergency declaration to justify a bailout. They would know that the current Supreme Court majority would be unlikely to block an emergency declaration by the executive branch and central bank. [ Annie Lowr ] ey: The AI bubble is no ordinary bubble The bailout authority is a loaded gun. Once triggered, it would bring downsides that have become familiar since 2008: public deficits and debt that devour GDP, zombie companies that taxpayers are forced to carry, an expansion of wealth inequality, and a dramatic shift of losses from perpetrators to the public. In Trump’s hands, it would also feature a new and more frightening dynamic: the creation of a standing money printer that can be turned on for the president’s allies and turned off for his enemies, enabling state-supported favoritism and plunder on a staggering scale. H istorically, the rationale for a bailout was that central banks should play the role of what Walter Bagehot called the “lender of last resort,” extending loans as necessary to tide over a blameless firm—a firm that, but for circumstances beyond its control, would otherwise be solvent and able to post adequate collateral. In 1932, Congress put this function inside the Federal Reserve. Section 13(3) of the Federal Reserve Act gave the central bank the power to extend loans to banks and any corporate entity in “unusual and exigent circumstances.” During the Great Depression, the Fed made limited use of its new authority. Then, for seven decades, Section 13(3) sat idle. The 2008 crash inaugurated the modern bailout era. When that crisis hit, its scale was unprecedented; financial markets had grown, becoming more intertwined and complex. The Federal Reserve, under Chairman Ben Bernanke, deemed the situation “urgent and exigent” and used Section 13(3) to establish special-purpose vehicles to buy up financial assets. Section 13(3) was also used to justify loans to AIG, an insurance company, and its affiliates, in exchange for collateral that consisted of nonperforming financial instruments with dubious market value. Working closely with the Treasury, which had related legal authority under the vague goal of dollar stability, the Federal Reserve began a program of extending loans to banks and other financial firms while purchasing huge quantities of mortgages and other shaky assets held by such entities as credit-card companies and private student-loan lenders. I served as a Federal Reserve governor during the tail end of the financial crisis, and then as the deputy secretary of the Treasury in the Obama administration. I eventually came to see that the bailout of the financial sector was not doing much for the broader economy. Long after the financial sector had recovered, many Americans were out of work, unable to repay their mortgages, and contending with rapacious debt collectors and sloppy mortgage servicers. Ordinary people could not help themselves to the enormous sampling of bailout options that the Federal Reserve and Treasury had provided to the banks. Mortgage-relief programs were slow to get off the ground and undermined by arguments that the intended recipients never should have had access to subprime loans in the first place. Congress passed the Dodd-Frank Act, a financial-reform bill, in part to address the distributional consequences of what had just happened and to limit the Federal Reserve’s emergency powers. Ultimately, however, the law left largely intact the Fed’s discretion to choose bailout recipients, the interest rate charged on bailout loans, and the quality and value of the collateral taken to backstop those loans. A decade later, when the coronavirus pandemic threatened an economic slowdown, the Federal Reserve mobilized preemptively. It initiated an even more aggressive version of large-scale asset purchases, with earlier money and more of it. Chairman Jerome Powell’s bailout opened up all of the faucets that spurt out continuous liquidity and created some new ones. Expanding its usage of Section 13(3) beyond mortgage assets, the Fed purchased the debts of various companies. In many cases, no requirements were imposed on these firms in exchange for cheap financing. By the Federal Reserve’s own estimates, the highly indebted fossil-fuel industry, for example, reaped more than $1.47 billion from the Main Street Lending Program—8.4 percent of the allocated funds—after lobbying the Fed to make the terms of its loans more generous. The Fed’s purchases of this debt “took all the risk overhang you normally associate with a risky company and took it off the table,” one chief investment officer told The Wall Street Journal at the time. By the time Silicon Valley Bank suddenly failed, in 2023, the Federal Reserve had learned that it could bail out favored sectors without imposing any consequences on failed businesses. Even though no one would have described this midsize regional bank as a “too big to fail” institution, the Federal Reserve and Treasury drew on the techniques they had perfected during the financial crisis and the pandemic. They established the Bank Term Funding Program to lend against collateral with depressed values. Interest rates were set so low as to permit any eligible entity to borrow from the Fed rather than the private sector, even after the threat of any deposit run had subsided. The result of these three bailouts was a collective recognition that the Federal Reserve had the power to choose winners and losers. Big banks and oil companies could be winners, the crypto sector and Silicon Valley–backed venture firms could be winners, and the CEOs and owners of these entities could be winners—even if they had acted recklessly. Families who had lost their homes and their incomes would be losers; so would entrepreneurs who aspired to displace companies that, but for a bailout, would have gone under. This approach widened income and wealth inequality, further shrinking the middle class. The companies that had been bailed out continued to act in ways that had permitted them to shed their costs to the public. In each case, these bailouts were conducted hastily, because of the unchallenged view that allowing companies or sectors to collapse would deprive the economy of necessary public benefits. And they were conducted with little consideration of their long-term consequences. T he recent history of bailouts gives us a clear indication of what the next one will look like. Enormous public money will be spent, in magnitudes approaching or exceeding the amount that Congress appropriates as part of its fiscal functions. The Federal Reserve and Treasury will once again choose the sectors that will benefit, and the terms on which bailouts will be offered. Only this time, the process will be under the aegis of an administration that brazenly trades political favors for money and support. The government could buy up nonperforming debt from favored firms; more nonperforming debt could be unloaded by data-center financiers and family foundations headed by allies of the president. Once the bailout machine is turned on, businesses will line up to buy favorable terms in exchange for political contributions. Those that refuse to play this game would be left to fail. [ Listen: On the brink of global recession ] But this chaotic free-for-all is not inevitable. Congress created the government’s bailout powers, and Congress can constrain them. If it does not, then it will be implicated in the consequences. If no public benefit justifies reviving a failing firm, then Congress should allow it to fail. If failing companies are going to be rescued, then conditions must be attached to bailout funds to make sure that the public benefit will be achieved. Congress should structure these terms before the next bailout. If the businesses being bailed out are data centers, for example, Congress could require them to limit their emissions or build their own renewable-energy sources. If the businesses being bailed out are the creators of frontier AI models, they could be required to prioritize investments in medical research. To make these judgments, Congress could establish a bailout manager to identify the public benefit, establish the conditions needed for the benefit to be delivered, and then oversee adherence to those conditions long after the crisis has passed. Every bailout is a sign of economic failure. Without interventions by our elected representatives, future bailouts won’t just risk widening inequality—they stand to politicize our entire economic system. A president who wields the bailout gun on his own behalf could leave the country with societal damage that will take generations to remediate. It’s up to Congress to assess those dangers now and determine how to intervene, while it still has the chance.

items.title: Obama mocks Trump’s government-wide response to Cheesecake Factory remark ahead of US midterms
items.description: Former US president Barack Obama on Wednesday mocked President Donald Trump for mobilising a government-wide response to his earlier remark that Trump had “got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory ”. “The White House even called the Secretary of Treasury,” Obama remarked, as he continued his campaign ahead of the congressional races in the US. Obama quipped, “This is the man who is in charge of the economy. The person who’s supposed to be figuring out how to make your life more affordable… They told him he should hold a press conference in front of the Cheesecake Factory.” Trump defended his White House decor and said Obama left the property deteriorated. “The White House, I think, is the number one symbol of our country, and we can’t have a White House with broken windows, with broken stone that hasn’t been painted in 30 years,” Trump said in Ohio. Neither man is on the ballot, but Republican President Trump and Democratic former president Obama took prominent roles on the campaign trail on Wednesday, with less than a week to go before congressional races that could shift the balance of power in Washington. While Trump has been on a weeks-long campaign blitz that has underlined Republican concerns about losing control of Congress for the final two years of his presidency, Obama had kept a relatively low public profile until the past week, during which he has delivered blistering speeches criticising Trump. Thirty-five of the 100 Senate seats and all 435 seats in the House of Representatives are being contested next Tuesday. Nonpartisan analysts generally favor Democrats’ chances of capturing a majority in the House, with the contest for the Senate seen as very close. On Wednesday, Obama appeared in Morrow, Georgia, near Atlanta, where he urged voters to support Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, who faces a challenge from Representative Mike Collins, a Republican. While delivering the standard Democratic critique of Trump for imposing tariffs and going to war in Iran, Obama also said America’s values were on the ballot, as he recalled the vision of slain civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., who is buried in Atlanta. “There is a moral component to the choices we face right now,” Obama said. “We are not going to fix the system that’s broken, we’re not going to unrig our economy, so long as we’ve got a culture where anything goes, where people in the highest offices of the land think it’s OK to lie and cheat and bully, if we continue to have a culture where money is deemed the only measure of our worth,” Obama said. Trump’s public approval rating has fallen to a near record low, with Americans increasingly sour on the high cost of living and the Iran war , but he remains an animating force in the party and has campaigned hard to increase Republican turnout. Americans have been voting for weeks, with 40 million ballots already cast, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab. A total of 45.9 million Americans voted early in the last midterm elections in 2022. Addressing a rally inside a modest college gymnasium in the Ohio town of Chillicothe, the president appeared with Senator Jon Husted of Ohio as he faces a challenge from Democratic former senator Sherrod Brown. Trump attacked Brown for supporting immigration policies the president said had overwhelmed Springfield, Ohio, with Haitian migrants. “The town went to hell,” he said. Trump spread false claims during the 2024 presidential campaign that Haitian immigrants in Springfield were eating cats and dogs, allegations local officials repeatedly said were untrue. Trump faces protesters Enthusiastic crowds have cheered Trump at rallies throughout the campaign, but hundreds of protesters lined Trump’s motorcade route in rural Chillicothe, raising banners that read, “Republican against Trump,” “Grab them by the ballot” and “GOP: Guardians of pedophiles.” During the rally, protesters interrupted Trump several times, including at least one who shouted about deceased convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein . “I threw Jeffrey Epstein the hell out of Mar-a-Lago,” Trump said in response. Trump and Epstein socialised in the 1990s and early 2000s, but Trump has said they later had a falling out and that he barred Epstein from Mar-a-Lago, Trump’s private club in Palm Beach, Florida. Justice Department releases from the Epstein files have included references to Trump, as well as many other prominent figures. The department has cautioned that some materials contain allegations that were unverified or uncorroborated. Protesters have interrupted Trump at virtually all his recent rallies. He typically accuses them of being paid protesters as they are carted off by security. Alaska, Michigan races Democrats will need to pick up seats in traditionally Republican-leaning states such as Ohio, Iowa or Alaska to overcome the current 53-47 Republican majority in the Senate. The New York Times reported that aides to Mary Peltola, the Senate Democratic nominee in Alaska, worked with the campaign’s lawyers and senior staff at Senate Democrats campaign arm to recruit two candidates who are on the ballot and could siphon votes from incumbent Republican US Senator Dan Sullivan. Representatives for Peltola did not immediately respond to requests for comment. “Mary Peltola should resign from the race. I think she should be criminally prosecuted for what she did,” Trump told reporters before departing for Ohio. In Michigan, where Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed are locked in a tight race for the Senate seat being vacated by Democratic Senator Gary Peters, both campaigns are relying on high-profile allies to energise supporters and boost turnout. Rogers spent the day campaigning with Senator Ted Cruz of Texas on a four-stop bus tour culminating in Imlay City, a small community northeast of Detroit. El-Sayed, meanwhile, was scheduled to join Peters and fellow Michigan Senator Elissa Slotkin for an evening canvassing rally in Downriver, southwest of Detroit.
